translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 275
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 275

sentences.zh: 【後唐紀四】　起柔兆閹茂四月，盡強圉大淵獻六月，凡一年有奇。

translations.literal: [Later Tang Annals, Part Four] Beginning in the fourth month of Rouzhao Yanmao, ending in the sixth month of Qiangyu Dayuanxian—in all, a little more than one year.
translations.idiomatic: [Annals of Later Tang, Part Four] From the fourth month of the first cyclical year through the sixth month of the next—altogether a little more than one year.

sentences.zh: 明宗聖德和武欽孝皇帝上之下天成元年（

translations.literal: Emperor Mingzong, Sagely in Virtue, Harmonious in Martial Prowess, and Reverent in Filial Piety—upper section, lower part; first year of Tiancheng (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong the Sagely, Harmonious, Martial, and Filial—continued; first year of Tiancheng (

sentences.zh: 丙戌，公元九二六年）

translations.literal: bingxu, corresponding to 926 CE)

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁亥朔，嚴辦將發，騎兵陳於宣仁門外，步兵陳於五鳳門外。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day of the month (dinghai), with preparations for departure complete, the cavalry were drawn up outside the Xuaren Gate and the infantry outside the Wufeng Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the first day of the fourth month, with everything ready for the imperial departure, cavalry formed up outside the Xuaren Gate and infantry outside the Wufeng Gate.

sentences.zh: 從馬直指揮使郭從謙不知睦王存乂已死，欲奉之以作亂，帥所部兵自營中露刃大呼，與黃甲兩軍攻興教門。

translations.literal: Guo Congqian, commander of the Imperial Horse Guard, not knowing that Prince Mu Li Cunyi was already dead, wished to install him and raise a rebellion; he led his troops from camp with bared blades, shouting loudly, and together with the two Yellow Armor armies attacked the Xingjiao Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Congqian, commander of the Imperial Horse Guard, did not know that Prince Mu Li Cunyi was already dead. Intending to set him on the throne and rebel, he led his men from camp with swords drawn, shouting, and joined the two Yellow Armor corps in an assault on the Xingjiao Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝方食，聞變，帥諸王及近衛騎兵擊之，逐亂兵出門，時蕃漢馬步使朱守殷將騎兵在外，帝遣中使急召之，欲與同擊賊；

translations.literal: The emperor was at his meal when he heard of the disturbance; he led the princes and the close-guard cavalry to strike them and drove the mutineers out through the gate. At that time Zhu Shouyin, commissioner of Tangut and Han horse and foot, was outside with the cavalry. The emperor sent a palace envoy to summon him urgently, wishing to attack the rebels together with him;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still eating when word of the uprising reached him. He led the princes and his personal cavalry to repel the attackers and drove the mutineers out of the gate. Zhu Shouyin, commissioner of the mixed Tangut and Han horse and foot forces, was outside with the cavalry, and the emperor sent a palace envoy to summon him at once, intending to strike the rebels together;

sentences.zh: 守殷不至，引兵憩於北邙茂林之下。

translations.literal: Shouyin did not come but led his troops to rest beneath the dense woods of North Mang.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyin never came. Instead he withdrew his troops to rest in the thick groves of North Mang.

sentences.zh: 亂兵焚興教門，緣城而入，近臣宿將皆釋甲潛遁，獨散員都指揮使李彥卿及宿衛軍校何福進、王全斌等十餘人力戰。

translations.literal: The mutineers burned the Xingjiao Gate and climbed in along the wall. The emperor's close attendants and veteran generals all cast off their armor and slipped away in secret; only Li Yanqing, commander of the scattered guards, and more than ten officers of the palace guard such as He Fujin and Wang Quanbin fought on with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels set fire to the Xingjiao Gate and scaled the wall to enter. The emperor's intimates and seasoned commanders all threw off their armor and fled in secret. Only Li Yanqing, commander of the scattered guards, and a dozen or so palace-guard officers including He Fujin and Wang Quanbin kept fighting.

sentences.zh: 俄而帝為流矢所中，鷹坊人善友扶帝自門樓下，至絳霄廡下，抽矢，渴懣求水，皇后不自省視，遣宦者進酪，須臾，帝殂。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor was struck by a stray arrow. Shan You, a man of the hawk yard, supported the emperor down from the gate tower to beneath the Jiangxiao colonnade, drew out the arrow, and in thirst and distress begged for water. The empress did not come to see him herself but sent a eunuch with kumiss; in a moment the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a stray arrow struck the emperor. Shan You of the hawk yard helped him down from the gate tower to the Jiangxiao colonnade, pulled out the arrow, and in agony cried for water. The empress never came to his side but sent a eunuch with fermented mare's milk; within moments the emperor was dead.

sentences.zh: 李彥卿等慟哭而去，左右皆散，善友斂廡下樂器覆帝屍而焚之。

translations.literal: Li Yanqing and the others wept bitterly and departed; those at the emperor's side all scattered. Shan You gathered musical instruments from beneath the colonnade, covered the emperor's corpse with them, and burned it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanqing and the rest wept and withdrew; everyone around the emperor fled. Shan You piled instruments from the colonnade over the body and set it ablaze.

sentences.zh: 彥卿，存審之子；

translations.literal: Yanqing was the son of Li Cunshen;
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing was a son of Li Cunshen;

sentences.zh: 福進、全斌放皆太原人也。

translations.literal: Fujin, Quanbin, and Fang were all men of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fujin, Quanbin, and Fang were all natives of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 劉後囊金寶繫馬鞍，與申王存屋及李紹榮引七百騎，焚喜慶殿，自師子門出走。

translations.literal: Empress Liu packed gold and jewels into saddlebags, and with Prince Shen Li Cunwu and Li Shaorong led seven hundred horsemen, burned the Xiqing Hall, and fled out through the Shizi Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liu loaded gold and jewels onto her saddle and, with Prince Shen Li Cunwu and Li Shaorong, led seven hundred horsemen, set fire to the Xiqing Hall, and escaped through the Shizi Gate.

sentences.zh: 通王存確、雅王存紀奔南山。

translations.literal: Prince Tong Li Cunque and Prince Ya Li Cunji fled to the Southern Hills.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tong Li Cunque and Prince Ya Li Cunji fled into the Southern Hills.

sentences.zh: 宮人多逃散，朱守殷入宮，選宮人三十餘人，各令自取樂器珍玩，內於其家。

translations.literal: Many palace women scattered in flight. Zhu Shouyin entered the palace, selected more than thirty palace women, had each take musical instruments and precious curios for herself, and kept them in his house.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women fled in all directions. Zhu Shouyin entered the palace, chose more than thirty of them, and had each help herself to instruments and valuables, which he then kept in his own residence.

sentences.zh: 於是諸軍大掠都城。

translations.literal: Thereupon the various armies plundered the capital on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: The armies then looted the capital on a vast scale.

sentences.zh: 是日，李嗣源至罌子谷，聞之，慟哭，謂諸將曰：「主上素得士心，正為群小蔽惑至此，今吾將安歸乎！

translations.literal: That day Li Siyuan reached Yingzi Valley; when he heard the news he wailed and said to his generals, "Our lord always won the hearts of his men; it was only because petty men deluded and misled him that things came to this. Where can I go now!
translations.idiomatic: That same day Li Siyuan reached Yingzi Valley. When he heard what had happened he wept aloud and told his generals, "Our sovereign always had the loyalty of his soldiers; petty men blinded him and brought him to this pass. Where am I to turn now!

sentences.zh: 」戊子，朱守殷遣使馳白嗣源，以「京城大亂，諸軍焚掠不已，願亟來救之！

translations.literal: " On the day wuzi, Zhu Shouyin sent a messenger at full gallop to inform Siyuan that "the capital is in great disorder and the armies are burning and plundering without cease; we beg you to come quickly to save it!
translations.idiomatic: " On wuzi day Zhu Shouyin sent a rider to tell Siyuan, "The capital is in chaos and the troops are still burning and looting without end—we beg you to come at once and restore order!

sentences.zh: 」乙丑，嗣源入洛陽，止於私第，禁焚掠，拾莊宗骨於灰燼之中而殯之。

translations.literal: " On the day yichou, Siyuan entered Luoyang, lodged at his private residence, forbade burning and plundering, gathered Zhuangzong's bones from the ashes, and gave them burial.
translations.idiomatic: " On yichou day Siyuan entered Luoyang, stayed at his private house, prohibited looting and arson, recovered Zhuangzong's bones from the ashes, and laid them to rest.

sentences.zh: 嗣源之入鄴也，前直指揮使平遙侯益脫身歸洛陽，莊宗撫之流涕。

translations.literal: When Siyuan had entered Ye, Hou Yi, former commander of the Direct Advance Guard and Marquis of Pingyao, had escaped and returned to Luoyang; Zhuangzong embraced him and wept.
translations.idiomatic: When Siyuan marched on Ye, Hou Yi, former commander of the Direct Advance Guard and Marquis of Pingyao, had slipped away and returned to Luoyang, where Zhuangzong embraced him in tears.

sentences.zh: 至是，益自縛請罪；

translations.literal: At this time Yi bound himself and asked to be punished;
translations.idiomatic: Now Yi came forward bound in cords to accept punishment;

sentences.zh: 嗣源曰：「樂為臣盡節，又何罪也！

translations.literal: Siyuan said, "You were glad to serve your lord with full loyalty—what crime is there in that!
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan said, "You served your sovereign faithfully with a willing heart—what fault is that!

sentences.zh: 」使復其職。

translations.literal: " and had him restored to his post.
translations.idiomatic: " and restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 嗣源謂朱守殷曰：「公善巡徼，以待魏王。

translations.literal: Siyuan said to Zhu Shouyin, "Sir, keep good watch on patrol and await the Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan told Zhu Shouyin, "Keep the patrols strong and wait for the Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 淑妃、德妃在宮，供給尤宜豐備。

translations.literal: The Shufei and Defei are in the palace; their provisions should especially be ample.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts Shu and De are still in the palace—see that they are especially well provided for.

sentences.zh: 吾俟山陵畢，社稷有奉，則歸籓為國家扞御北方耳。

translations.literal: When the imperial tomb rites are finished and the altars of state have a lord, I shall return to my fief and defend the north for the realm, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Once the burial is complete and the realm has a ruler, I mean only to return to my fief and guard the northern frontier for the state.

sentences.zh: 」是日，豆盧革帥百官上箋勸進，嗣源面諭之曰：「吾奉詔討賊，不幸部曲叛散；

translations.literal: " That day Doulu Ge led the officials in submitting a memorial urging him to ascend the throne. Siyuan addressed them in person and said, "I received the edict to punish the rebels, but unfortunately my troops mutinied and scattered;
translations.idiomatic: " That day Doulu Ge led the civil officials in a memorial urging him to take the throne. Siyuan told them face to face, "I was ordered to punish the rebels, but my troops mutinied and broke apart;

sentences.zh: 欲入朝自訴，又為紹榮所隔，披猖至此。

translations.literal: I wished to enter court and plead my case, but was blocked by Shaorong and driven to this wild pass.
translations.idiomatic: I meant to return to court and explain myself, but Shaorong barred my way and I was swept to this extremity.

sentences.zh: 吾本無他心，諸群遽爾見推，殊非相悉，願勿言也！

translations.literal: I never had any other intent; that you gentlemen should so hastily urge me on shows you do not truly know me—please say no more of it!
translations.idiomatic: I never harbored any other design. That you should press me so suddenly shows you do not know me at all—I beg you to speak of it no further!

sentences.zh: 」革等固請，嗣源不許。

translations.literal: " Ge and the others pressed him firmly, but Siyuan would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: " Ge and the rest pressed him again, but Siyuan refused.

sentences.zh: 李紹榮欲奔河中就永王存霸，從兵稍散；

translations.literal: Li Shaorong wished to flee to Hezhong and join Prince Yong Li Cunba, but his followers gradually dispersed;
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaorong tried to reach Hezhong and Prince Yong Li Cunba, but his escort slowly melted away;

sentences.zh: 庚寅，至平陸，止餘數騎，為人所執，折足送洛陽。

translations.literal: on the day gengyin he reached Pinglu with only a few horsemen left, was seized by others, had his legs broken, and was sent to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: on gengyin day he reached Pinglu with only a handful of riders left, was captured, had his legs broken, and was sent to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 存霸亦帥眾千人棄鎮奔晉陽。

translations.literal: Cunba also led a thousand men, abandoned his post, and fled to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cunba likewise abandoned his command with a thousand men and fled to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，魏王繼岌至興平，聞洛陽亂，復引兵而西，謀保據鳳翔。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, Prince of Wei Li Jiji reached Xingping; hearing of the disorder in Luoyang, he turned his army west again and planned to hold Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day Prince of Wei Li Jiji reached Xingping. When he heard of the chaos in Luoyang he marched west again, intending to secure Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 向延嗣至鳳翔，以莊宗之命誅李紹琛。

translations.literal: Xiang Yansi reached Fengxiang and, by Zhuangzong's order, executed Li Shaochen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yansi reached Fengxiang and, acting on Zhuangzong's orders, put Li Shaochen to death.

sentences.zh: 初，莊宗命呂、鄭二內養在晉陽，一監兵，一監倉庫，自留守張憲以以下皆承應不暇。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhuangzong had placed two palace stewards, Lü and Zheng, at Taiyuan—one to supervise the troops and one the storehouses—and from the regent Zhang Xian downward everyone was kept busy answering to them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhuangzong had stationed two palace stewards, Lü and Zheng, at Taiyuan—one over the troops and one over the granaries—and from regent Zhang Xian down everyone was kept scrambling to obey them.

sentences.zh: 及鄴都有變，又命汾州刺史李彥超為北都巡檢。

translations.literal: When Ye Capital rose in revolt, he also appointed Li Yanchao, prefect of Fenzhou, as inspector of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye rebelled he further appointed Li Yanchao, prefect of Fenzhou, inspector of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 彥超，彥卿之兄也。

translations.literal: Yanchao was Yanqing's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao was the elder brother of Yanqing.

sentences.zh: 莊宗既殂，推官河間張昭遠勸張憲奉表勸進，憲曰：「吾一書生，自布衣至服金紫，皆出先帝之恩，豈可偷生而不自愧乎！

translations.literal: After Zhuangzong died, Zhang Zhaoyuan of Hejian, a legal officer, urged Zhang Xian to submit a memorial urging Siyuan to ascend the throne. Xian said, "I am but a scholar; from common cloth to wearing gold and purple, all came from the late emperor's grace—how could I cling to life without shame!
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong's death Zhang Zhaoyuan of Hejian, a legal officer, urged Zhang Xian to submit a memorial urging Siyuan to take the throne. Xian said, "I am only a scholar. From commoner to court rank, everything I have came from the late emperor's grace—how could I save my skin and not feel ashamed!

sentences.zh: 」昭遠泣曰：「此古人所行，公能行之，忠義不朽矣。

translations.literal: " Zhaoyuan wept and said, "This is what the ancients did; if you can do it, your loyalty and righteousness will never perish.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhaoyuan wept and said, "That is what the ancients did. If you can do the same, your loyalty will live forever.

sentences.zh: 」有李存沼者，莊宗之近屬，自洛陽奔晉陽，矯傳莊宗之命，陰與二內養謀殺憲及彥超，據晉陽拒守。

translations.literal: " There was one Li Cunzhao, a close kinsman of Zhuangzong, who fled from Luoyang to Taiyuan, forged Zhuangzong's orders, and secretly plotted with the two palace stewards to kill Xian and Yanchao, seize Taiyuan, and hold it in resistance.
translations.idiomatic: " A kinsman of Zhuangzong named Li Cunzhao fled from Luoyang to Taiyuan, forged orders in Zhuangzong's name, and secretly joined the two stewards in a plot to kill Xian and Yanchao and hold Taiyuan in defiance.

sentences.zh: 彥超知之，密告憲，欲先圖之。

translations.literal: Yanchao learned of it, secretly informed Xian, and wished to strike first.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao learned of the plot, told Xian in secret, and wanted to move against them first.

sentences.zh: 憲曰：「僕受先帝厚恩，不忍為此。

translations.literal: Xian said, "I received great favor from the late emperor and cannot bear to do this.
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "The late emperor showed me great kindness—I cannot bring myself to do that.

sentences.zh: 徇義而不免於禍，乃天也。

translations.literal: To follow righteousness and still not escape disaster—that is Heaven's will.
translations.idiomatic: If loyalty still brings ruin, that is Heaven's decree.

sentences.zh: 」彥超謀未決，壬辰夜，軍士共殺二內養及存沼於牙城，因大掠達旦。

translations.literal: " Before Yanchao's plan was settled, on the night of the day renchen the soldiers together killed the two palace stewards and Cunzhao at the headquarters city and then plundered on a great scale until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: " Before Yanchao could decide, on the night of renchen day the troops together killed the two stewards and Cunzhao at headquarters, then looted until dawn.

sentences.zh: 憲聞變，出奔忻州。

translations.literal: When Xian heard of the disturbance he fled to Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian heard of the uprising he fled to Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 會嗣源移書至，彥超號令士卒，城中始安，遂權知太原軍府。

translations.literal: When Siyuan's letter of transfer arrived, Yanchao gave orders to the soldiers, the city at last grew calm, and he thereupon acted as provisional administrator of the Taiyuan military prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When a letter from Siyuan arrived, Yanchao brought the troops to order and the city finally settled; he then took provisional charge of the Taiyuan military government.

sentences.zh: 百官三箋請嗣源監國，嗣源乃許之。

translations.literal: The officials submitted three memorials asking Siyuan to oversee the state, and Siyuan then consented.
translations.idiomatic: The officials submitted three memorials asking Siyuan to serve as regent, and at last he agreed.

sentences.zh: 甲午，入居興聖宮，始受百官班見。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu he moved into the Xingsheng Palace and for the first time received the officials in formal audience.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day he took up residence in the Xingsheng Palace and for the first time received the officials in formal audience.

sentences.zh: 下令稱教，百官稱之曰殿下。

translations.literal: His orders were styled "edicts," and the officials addressed him as Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: His orders were issued as edicts, and the officials addressed him as Your Highness.

sentences.zh: 莊宗後宮存者猶千餘人，宣徽使選其美少者數百獻於監國，監國曰：「奚用此為！

translations.literal: Of Zhuangzong's rear palace more than a thousand women still survived. The commissioner of the Palace Secretariat selected several hundred of the young and beautiful and presented them to the regent. The regent said, "What use is there for this!
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand women of Zhuangzong's harem still survived. The palace commissioner chose several hundred of the young and fair and presented them to the regent. He said, "What need is there for this!

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「宮中職掌不可闕也。

translations.literal: " The reply was, "The palace offices cannot be left vacant.
translations.idiomatic: " They answered, "The palace offices cannot be left empty.

sentences.zh: 」監國曰：「宮中職掌宜諳故事，此輩安知！

translations.literal: " The regent said, "Palace offices should be filled by those versed in precedent—what do these know!
translations.idiomatic: " The regent said, "Palace posts should go to those who know court precedent—what do these girls know!

sentences.zh: 」乃悉用老舊之人補之，其少年者皆出歸其親戚，無親戚者任其所適。

translations.literal: " He then filled all the posts with old and experienced persons; the young women were all released to return to their kin, and those without kin were free to go where they wished.
translations.idiomatic: " He filled every post with experienced veterans of the palace. The young women were sent back to their families, and those without families were free to marry as they chose.

sentences.zh: 蜀中所送宮人亦准此。

translations.literal: The palace women sent from Shu were treated by the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: The palace women sent from Shu were treated the same way.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以中門使安重誨為樞密使，鎮州別駕張延朗為副使。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, An Chonghui, commissioner of the Central Gate, was made chief palace secretary, and Zhang Yanlang, vice-prefect of Zhenzhou, was made deputy.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day An Chonghui, commissioner of the Central Gate, was appointed chief palace secretary, and Zhang Yanlang, vice-prefect of Zhenzhou, deputy secretary.

sentences.zh: 延朗，開封人也，仕梁為租庸吏，性纖巧，善事權要，以女妻重誨之子，故重誨引之。

translations.literal: Yanlang was a man of Kaifeng who had served Liang as a rent-and-corvée clerk; he was subtle and clever by nature, skilled at courting the powerful, and because he gave his daughter in marriage to Chonghui's son, Chonghui brought him forward.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang was from Kaifeng and had served the Liang as a rent-and-corvée clerk. Subtle and adroit, he knew how to please men of power; he married his daughter to Chonghui's son, and on that account Chonghui advanced him.

sentences.zh: 監國令所在訪求諸王。

translations.literal: The regent ordered that the princes be sought everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: The regent ordered a search for the princes throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 通王存確、雅王存紀匿民間，或密告安重誨，重誨與李紹真謀曰：「今殿下既監國典喪，諸王宜早為之所，以壹人心。

translations.literal: Prince Tong Li Cunque and Prince Ya Li Cunji hid among the common people. Someone secretly informed An Chonghui, and Chonghui plotted with Li Shaozhen, saying, "Now that Your Highness oversees the state and presides over the mourning, the princes should be dealt with early to settle men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tong Li Cunque and Prince Ya Li Cunji were hiding among the people. Someone secretly informed An Chonghui, who plotted with Li Shaozhen: "Your Highness now serves as regent and presides over the funeral. The princes should be settled quickly so that hearts may be united.

sentences.zh: 殿下性慈，不可以聞。

translations.literal: Your Highness is gentle by nature and must not hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness is too gentle—he must not be told.

sentences.zh: 」乃密遣人就田舍殺之。

translations.literal: " He then secretly sent men to their farmsteads to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: " He secretly sent men to their hiding places in the countryside and had them killed.

sentences.zh: 後月餘，監國乃聞之，切責重誨，傷惜久之。

translations.literal: More than a month later the regent heard of it, rebuked Chonghui sharply, and grieved over it for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month passed before the regent learned of it. He rebuked Chonghui severely and mourned the princes for a long while.

sentences.zh: 劉皇后與申王存渥奔晉陽，在道與存渥私通。

translations.literal: Empress Liu and Prince Shen Li Cunwo fled to Taiyuan and on the road had a secret liaison with Cunwo.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liu fled to Taiyuan with Prince Shen Li Cunwo and took him as her lover on the road.

sentences.zh: 存渥至晉陽，李彥超不納，走至鳳谷，為其下所殺。

translations.literal: When Cunwo reached Taiyuan, Li Yanchao would not admit him; he fled to Fenggu and was killed by his own followers.
translations.idiomatic: When Cunwo reached Taiyuan, Li Yanchao refused him entry. He fled to Fenggu, where his own men killed him.

sentences.zh: 明日，永王存霸亦至晉陽，從兵逃散俱盡，存霸削髮、僧服謁李彥超，「願為山僧，幸垂庇護。

translations.literal: The next day Prince Yong Li Cunba also reached Taiyuan; his followers had all scattered in flight. Cunba shaved his head, put on monk's robes, and called on Li Yanchao, saying, "I wish to become a mountain monk; I beg your protection.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Prince Yong Li Cunba also reached Taiyuan. His escort had entirely dispersed. He shaved his head, dressed as a monk, and begged Li Yanchao, "Let me live as a mountain monk—please shelter me.

sentences.zh: 」軍士爭欲殺之，彥超曰：「六相公來，當奏取進止。

translations.literal: " The soldiers vied to kill him. Yanchao said, "The Sixth Prince has come; I must memorialize and await instructions.
translations.idiomatic: " The troops clamored to kill him. Yanchao said, "The Sixth Prince has arrived—I must report to the court and await orders.

sentences.zh: 」軍士不聽，殺之於府門碑下。

translations.literal: " The soldiers would not listen and killed him beneath the stele at the prefectural gate.
translations.idiomatic: " The soldiers would not wait and killed him beneath the stele at the gate of headquarters.

sentences.zh: 劉皇后為尼於晉陽，監國使人就殺之。

translations.literal: Empress Liu became a nun at Taiyuan; the regent sent men to kill her there.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liu became a nun at Taiyuan; the regent sent men to put her to death.

sentences.zh: 薛王存禮及莊宗幼子繼嵩、繼潼、繼蟾繼嶢，遭亂皆不知所終。

translations.literal: Prince Xue Li Cunli and Zhuangzong's young sons Jisong, Jitong, Jichan, and Jiyao, caught in the disorder, all vanished without trace of their end.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xue Li Cunli and Zhuangzong's young sons Jisong, Jitong, Jichan, and Jiyao were lost in the chaos and never heard of again.

sentences.zh: 惟邕王存美以病風偏枯得免，居於晉陽。

translations.literal: Only Prince Yong Li Cunmei, being paralyzed by wind-stroke on one side of the body, was spared and lived at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Only Prince Yong Li Cunmei was spared, because he was paralyzed by stroke, and he remained at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 徐溫、高季興聞莊宗遇弒，益重嚴可求、梁震。

translations.literal: When Xu Wen and Gao Jixing heard that Zhuangzong had been assassinated, they valued Yan Keqiu and Liang Zhen all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Wen and Gao Jixing heard that Zhuangzong had been killed, they relied even more heavily on Yan Keqiu and Liang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 梁震薦前陵州判官貴平孫光憲於季興，使掌書記。

translations.literal: Liang Zhen recommended to Jixing Sun Guangxian of Guiping, former magistrate of Lingzhou, and had him take charge of secretarial duties.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zhen recommended Sun Guangxian of Guiping, former magistrate of Lingzhou, to Jixing and had him serve as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 季興大治戰艦，欲攻楚，光憲諫曰：「荊南亂離之後，賴公休息士民，始有生意。

translations.literal: Jixing greatly expanded his warships and wished to attack Chu. Guangxian remonstrated, saying, "After the turmoil and dispersal in Jingnan, it is thanks to you, my lord, that the soldiers and people have been given rest and life has begun to return.
translations.idiomatic: Jixing greatly expanded his fleet and planned to attack Chu. Guangxian remonstrated: "After the chaos in Jingnan, the people have only just begun to recover under your rule.

sentences.zh: 若又與楚國交惡，他國乘吾之弊，良可憂也。

translations.literal: If we again make enemies of Chu, other states will take advantage of our weakness—that is truly worrisome.
translations.idiomatic: If we turn hostile to Chu again, other states will seize on our weakness—that is deeply worrying.

sentences.zh: 」季興乃止。

translations.literal: " Jixing then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Jixing abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，李紹榮至洛陽，監國責之曰：「吾何負於爾，而殺吾兒！

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, Li Shaorong reached Luoyang. The regent rebuked him, saying, "What wrong have I done you, that you killed my son!
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day Li Shaorong reached Luoyang. The regent rebuked him: "What have I done to you, that you killed my son!

sentences.zh: 」紹榮瞋目直視曰：「先帝何負於爾？

translations.literal: " Shaorong glared and looked him straight in the eye, saying, "What wrong did the late emperor do you?
translations.idiomatic: " Shaorong glared straight at him and said, "What wrong did the late emperor do you?

sentences.zh: 」遂斬之，復其姓名曰元行欽。

translations.literal: " He was then beheaded, and his original name Yuan Xingqin was restored.
translations.idiomatic: " He was beheaded at once, and his original name Yuan Xingqin was restored.

sentences.zh: 監國恐征蜀軍還為變，以石敬瑭為陝州留後；

translations.literal: The regent feared that the army returning from the Shu campaign might turn mutinous and appointed Shi Jingtang acting prefect of Shaanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Fearing mutiny when the Shu expedition returned, the regent appointed Shi Jingtang acting prefect of Shaanzhou;

sentences.zh: 己亥，以李從珂為河中留後。

translations.literal: on the day jihai he appointed Li Congke acting prefect of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: on jihai day he appointed Li Congke acting prefect of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 樞密使張居翰乞歸田裡，許之。

translations.literal: Zhang Juhan, chief palace secretary, asked to return to his home district and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juhan, chief palace secretary, asked to retire to his home district and was allowed to do so.

sentences.zh: 李紹真屢薦孔循之才，庚子，以循為樞密副使。

translations.literal: Li Shaozhen repeatedly recommended Kong Xun's talent; on the day gengzi he appointed Xun deputy palace secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaozhen repeatedly praised Kong Xun's ability; on gengzi day Xun was made deputy palace secretary.

sentences.zh: 李紹宏請複姓馬。

translations.literal: Li Shaohong asked to resume the surname Ma.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaohong asked to restore his original surname Ma.

sentences.zh: 監國下教，數租庸使孔謙奸佞侵刻窮困軍民之罪而斬之，凡謙所立苛斂之法皆罷之，因廢租庸使及內勾司，依舊為鹽鐵、戶部、度支三司，委宰相一人專判。

translations.literal: The regent issued an edict recounting the crimes of Kong Qian, commissioner of rent and corvée—his treachery, flattery, oppression, and driving soldiers and civilians to destitution—and had him executed. All the harsh levies Qian had established were abolished. The office of rent-and-corvée commissioner and the internal audit bureau were done away with, and the three departments of Salt and Iron, Revenue, and Public Works were restored as before, with one chief minister placed in sole charge.
translations.idiomatic: The regent issued an edict listing the crimes of Kong Qian, commissioner of rent and corvée—his treachery, flattery, extortion, and ruin of soldiers and civilians—and had him executed. Every harsh levy Qian had created was abolished. The rent-and-corvée commission and the internal audit office were abolished, and the three traditional departments—Salt and Iron, Revenue, and Public Works—were restored under a single chief minister.

sentences.zh: 又罷諸道監軍使；

translations.literal: He also abolished the military supervisors in all circuits;
translations.idiomatic: He also abolished the military supervisors posted to every circuit;

sentences.zh: 以莊宗由宦官亡國，命諸道盡殺之。

translations.literal: because Zhuangzong's state had perished through eunuchs, he ordered that they be killed throughout all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: and because Zhuangzong's dynasty had fallen through the eunuchs, he ordered them killed in every circuit.

sentences.zh: 魏王繼岌自興平退至武功，宦者李從襲曰：「禍福未可知，退不如進，請王亟東行以救內難。

translations.literal: Prince of Wei Li Jiji withdrew from Xingping to Wugong. The eunuch Li Congxi said, "Fortune and disaster are still unknown; retreat is not as good as advance—I beg Your Highness to hurry east and rescue the inner turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei Li Jiji withdrew from Xingping to Wugong. The eunuch Li Congxi said, "Fortune is still uncertain—better to advance than retreat. I beg Your Highness to march east at once and relieve the capital.

sentences.zh: 」繼岌從之。

translations.literal: " Jiji followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiji agreed.

sentences.zh: 還，至渭水，權西都留守張籛已斷浮梁；

translations.literal: On the return he reached the Wei River; Zhang Qian, acting regent of the Western Capital, had already cut the pontoon bridge;
translations.idiomatic: On the march back he reached the Wei River, where Zhang Qian, acting regent of the Western Capital, had already destroyed the pontoon bridge;

sentences.zh: 循水浮渡，是日至渭南，腹心呂知柔等皆已竄匿。

translations.literal: they followed the water and crossed by raft; that day they reached Weinan. His trusted followers such as Lü Zhirou had all fled into hiding.
translations.idiomatic: they crossed on rafts along the river. That day they reached Weinan, where trusted aides such as Lü Zhirou had already gone into hiding.

sentences.zh: 從襲謂繼岌曰：「時事已去，王宜自圖。

translations.literal: Congxi said to Jiji, "The times are already gone; Your Highness should look to yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Congxi told Jiji, "The cause is lost. Your Highness must decide your own fate.

sentences.zh: 」繼岌徘徊流涕，乃自伏於床，命僕夫李環縊殺之。

translations.literal: " Jiji paced back and forth in tears, then lay down on his bed, ordered his servant Li Huan to strangle him, and died.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiji paced in tears, then lay down on his bed and ordered his servant Li Huan to strangle him.

sentences.zh: 任圜代將其眾而東。

translations.literal: Ren Huan took command of the army in his place and marched east.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Huan took command of the army and marched east.

sentences.zh: 監國命石敬瑭慰撫之，軍士皆無異言。

translations.literal: The regent ordered Shi Jingtang to comfort and reassure them; the soldiers all raised no objection.
translations.idiomatic: The regent sent Shi Jingtang to reassure the troops, and they raised no complaint.

sentences.zh: 先是，監國命所親李沖為華州都監，應接西師。

translations.literal: Earlier the regent had appointed his intimate Li Chong military supervisor of Hua Prefecture to receive the western army.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the regent had appointed his confidant Li Chong military supervisor of Hua Prefecture to receive the western army.

sentences.zh: 沖擅逼華州節度使史彥鎔入朝；

translations.literal: Chong on his own authority forced Shi Yanrong, military governor of Hua Prefecture, to enter court;
translations.idiomatic: Chong on his own authority forced Shi Yanrong, military governor of Hua, to go to court;

sentences.zh: 同州節度使李存敬過華州，沖殺之，並屠其家；

translations.literal: when Li Cunjing, military governor of Tong Prefecture, passed through Hua Prefecture, Chong killed him and slaughtered his household as well;
translations.idiomatic: when Li Cunjing, military governor of Tong, passed through Hua, Chong killed him and massacred his entire family;

sentences.zh: 又殺西川行營都監李從襲。

translations.literal: he also killed Li Congxi, military supervisor of the western Shu expedition.
translations.idiomatic: and he also killed Li Congxi, military supervisor of the western Shu expedition.

sentences.zh: 彥鎔泣訴於安重誨，重誨遣彥鎔還鎮，召沖歸朝。

translations.literal: Yanrong wept and appealed to An Chonghui; Chonghui sent Yanrong back to his post and summoned Chong to court.
translations.idiomatic: Yanrong wept before An Chonghui, who sent him back to his post and summoned Chong to court.

sentences.zh: 自監國入洛，內外機事皆決於李紹真。

translations.literal: From the time the regent entered Luoyang, all internal and external affairs of state were decided by Li Shaozhen.
translations.idiomatic: After the regent entered Luoyang, Li Shaozhen decided every matter of state, within the palace and without.

sentences.zh: 紹真擅收威勝節度使李紹欽、太子少保李紹沖下獄，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Shaozhen on his own authority seized Li Shaoqin, military governor of Weisheng, and Li Shaochong, junior guardian of the heir apparent, and put them in prison, intending to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozhen on his own authority arrested Li Shaoqin, military governor of Weisheng, and Li Shaochong, junior guardian of the heir apparent, and planned to execute them.

sentences.zh: 安重誨謂紹真曰：「溫、段罪惡皆在梁朝，今殿下新平內難，冀安萬國，豈專為公報仇邪！

translations.literal: An Chonghui said to Shaozhen, "The crimes of Wen and Duan all belong to the Liang dynasty. Now Your Highness has newly pacified the inner turmoil and hopes to settle the myriad states—how could this be solely to avenge you!
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui told Shaozhen, "Wen and Duan's crimes all date to the Liang. Your Highness has just quelled the capital crisis and hopes to bring peace to the realm—surely this is not meant only as your private revenge!

sentences.zh: 」紹真由是稍沮。

translations.literal: " Shaozhen was thereby somewhat discouraged.
translations.idiomatic: " Shaozhen relented somewhat.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，監國教，李紹沖、紹欽複姓名為溫韜、段凝，並放歸田裡。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou the regent issued an edict restoring Li Shaochong and Shaoqin to their original names Wen Tao and Duan Ning, and both were released to return to their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day the regent ordered Li Shaochong and Shaoqin restored to their original names Wen Tao and Duan Ning and sent home to their districts.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以孔循為樞密使。

translations.literal: On the day renyin, Kong Xun was made chief palace secretary.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day Kong Xun was appointed chief palace secretary.

sentences.zh: 有司議即位禮。

translations.literal: The responsible offices deliberated on the rites of accession.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices debated the rites of enthronement.

sentences.zh: 李紹真、孔循以為唐運已盡，宜自建國號。

translations.literal: Li Shaozhen and Kong Xun held that the fortune of Tang was exhausted and a new dynastic title should be established.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaozhen and Kong Xun argued that Tang's mandate was spent and a new dynastic name should be adopted.

sentences.zh: 監國問左右：「何謂國號？

translations.literal: The regent asked those at his side, "What is meant by a dynastic title?
translations.idiomatic: The regent asked his attendants, "What is a dynastic title?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「先帝賜姓于唐，為唐復仇，繼昭宗後，故稱唐。

translations.literal: " The reply was, "The late emperor received the surname from Tang, avenged Tang, and succeeded after Emperor Zhaozong—therefore we are called Tang.
translations.idiomatic: " They answered, "The late emperor took the Tang surname, avenged Tang, and succeeded Emperor Zhaozong—that is why we are called Tang.

sentences.zh: 今梁朝之人不欲殿下稱唐耳。

translations.literal: It is only that men of the former Liang do not wish Your Highness to be called Tang.
translations.idiomatic: It is only that former Liang officials do not want Your Highness to keep the name Tang.

sentences.zh: 」監國曰：「吾年十三事獻祖，獻祖以吾宗屬，視吾猶子。

translations.literal: " The regent said, "At thirteen I served Ancestor Xian; because I was of his clan, he treated me as a son.
translations.idiomatic: " The regent said, "At thirteen I entered the service of Ancestor Xian, who treated me as his own son because I was of his clan.

sentences.zh: 又事武皇垂三十年，先帝垂二十年，經綸攻戰，未嘗不預；

translations.literal: I also served Martial Emperor for nearly thirty years and the late emperor for nearly twenty; in planning campaigns and battles I was never left out;
translations.idiomatic: I served Martial Emperor for nearly thirty years and the late emperor for nearly twenty, sharing in every campaign and every plan;

sentences.zh: 武皇之基業則吾之基業也，先帝之天下則吾之天下也，安有同家而異國乎！

translations.literal: Martial Emperor's foundation is my foundation, and the late emperor's realm is my realm—how could one family have two states!
translations.idiomatic: Martial Emperor's foundation is my foundation, and the late emperor's realm is my realm—how could one household bear two dynastic names!

sentences.zh: 」令執政更議。

translations.literal: " He ordered the chief ministers to deliberate again.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the chief ministers to reconsider.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書李琪曰：「若改國號，則先帝遂為路人，梓宮安所托乎！

translations.literal: Li Qi, minister of personnel, said, "If the dynastic title is changed, the late emperor becomes a stranger—where would his coffin find its resting place!
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi, minister of personnel, said, "If we change the dynastic name, the late emperor becomes a stranger—where would his coffin rest!

sentences.zh: 不惟殿下忘三世舊君，吾曹為人臣者能自安乎！

translations.literal: Not only would Your Highness forget three generations of former lords—we as his ministers, could we rest easy!
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness would not only forget three generations of sovereigns—we as his ministers could never live with ourselves!

sentences.zh: 前代以旁支入繼多矣，宜用嗣子柩前即位之禮。

translations.literal: In former ages collateral lines succeeding to the throne were common; the rite of accession before the heir's coffin should be used.
translations.idiomatic: Collateral succession was common in earlier ages; we should use the rite of enthronement before the late emperor's coffin.

sentences.zh: 」眾從之。

translations.literal: " The assembly agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " All agreed.

sentences.zh: 丙午，監國自興聖宮赴西宮，服斬衰，於柩前即皇帝位，百官縞素。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu the regent went from the Xingsheng Palace to the Western Palace, wore the coarsest hemp mourning, and took the imperial throne before the coffin; the officials all wore white hemp.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day the regent went from the Xingsheng Palace to the Western Palace in the coarsest mourning garb and took the throne before the coffin while the officials wore white hemp.

sentences.zh: 既而御袞冕受冊，百官吉服稱賀。

translations.literal: Thereafter he assumed the imperial robes and cap, received the investiture, and the officials in auspicious dress offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: He then donned the imperial regalia, received the investiture, and the officials in court dress offered their congratulations.

sentences.zh: 戊申，敕中外之臣毋得獻鷹犬奇玩之類。

translations.literal: On the day wushen an edict forbade ministers within and without from presenting hawks, dogs, and curious treasures.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day an edict forbade all officials to present hawks, dogs, or exotic curios.

sentences.zh: 有司劾奏太原尹張憲委城之罪；

translations.literal: The responsible offices impeached Zhang Xian, prefect of Taiyuan, for the crime of abandoning the city;
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices impeached Zhang Xian, prefect of Taiyuan, for abandoning the city;

sentences.zh: 庚戌，賜憲死。

translations.literal: on the day gengxu he was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: on gengxu day the emperor ordered him executed.

sentences.zh: 任圜將征蜀兵二萬六千人至洛陽，明宗慰撫之，各令還營。

translations.literal: Ren Huan led the twenty-six thousand troops of the Shu expedition to Luoyang; Emperor Mingzong comforted them and ordered each to return to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Huan brought the twenty-six thousand troops of the Shu expedition to Luoyang. Emperor Mingzong reassured them and sent each unit back to its camp.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin there was a general amnesty and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day the emperor proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 量留後宮百人，宦官三十人，教坊百人，鷹坊二十人，御廚五十人，自餘任從所適。

translations.literal: A fixed number were kept in the rear palace: one hundred women, thirty eunuchs, one hundred in the music bureau, twenty in the hawk yard, fifty in the imperial kitchen; the rest were free to go where they wished.
translations.idiomatic: He retained one hundred palace women, thirty eunuchs, one hundred musicians, twenty hawk handlers, and fifty imperial cooks; the rest were free to go where they chose.

sentences.zh: 諸司使務有名無實者皆廢之。

translations.literal: All commissioner offices that existed in name only were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Every commissioner office that existed in name only was abolished.

sentences.zh: 分遣諸軍就食近畿，以省饋運。

translations.literal: The various armies were dispersed to be fed in the near capital region to save on transport of provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The armies were dispersed to forage in the capital region to save the cost of supply trains.

sentences.zh: 除夏、秋稅省耗。

translations.literal: The summer and autumn tax surcharges were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The summer and autumn tax surcharges were abolished.

sentences.zh: 節度、防禦等使，正、至、端午、降誕四節聽貢奉，毋得斂百姓；

translations.literal: Military governors, defense commissioners, and the like were permitted tribute offerings on the four festivals of New Year, Winter Solstice, Dragon Boat, and the emperor's birthday, but might not levy the common people;
translations.idiomatic: Military governors and defense commissioners might present tribute on New Year, Winter Solstice, Dragon Boat, and the emperor's birthday, but might not levy the people;

sentences.zh: 刺史以下不得貢奉。

translations.literal: prefects and below might not present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: prefects and lower ranks might not present tribute at all.

sentences.zh: 選入先遭塗毀文書者，令三銓止除詐偽，餘復舊規。

translations.literal: For candidates whose documents had previously been defaced, the three selection boards were ordered to eliminate only fraud; the rest were restored to the old rules.
translations.idiomatic: For candidates whose credentials had been defaced, the three selection boards were to reject only fraud; all other old rules were restored.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙辰朔，以太子賓客鄭玨、工部尚書任圜並為中書侍郎、同平章事；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the first day of the month (bingchen), Zheng Jue, guest of the heir apparent, and Ren Huan, minister of works, were both made vice grand councilor of the Secretariat and co-equal chief ministers;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the first day, Zheng Jue, guest of the heir apparent, and Ren Huan, minister of works, were both made vice grand councilor and co-equal chief minister;

sentences.zh: 圜仍判三司。

translations.literal: Huan still held charge of the three departments.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Huan continued to oversee the three fiscal departments.

sentences.zh: 圜憂公如家，簡拔賢俊，杜絕僥倖，期年之間，府庫充實，軍民皆足，朝綱粗立。

translations.literal: Huan cared for the public good as for his own household, selected worthy and able men, and shut out favor-seekers; within a year the treasuries were full, soldiers and civilians alike had enough, and court discipline was roughly established.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Huan treated the public treasury as his own household, promoted worthy men, and shut out favor-seekers. Within a year the coffers were full, soldiers and civilians were provided for, and court discipline was roughly restored.

sentences.zh: 圜每以天下為己任，由是安重誨忌之。

translations.literal: Huan took the realm as his personal charge, and for this An Chonghui resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ren Huan took the welfare of the realm as his personal charge, An Chonghui came to resent him.

sentences.zh: 武寧節度使李紹真、忠武節度使李紹瓊、貝州剌吏李紹英、齊州防禦使李紹虔、河陽節度使李紹奇、洺州刺史李紹能，各請復舊姓名為霍彥威、萇從簡、房知溫、王晏球、夏魯奇、米君立，許之。

translations.literal: Li Shaozhen, military governor of Wuning; Li Shaoqiong, military governor of Zhongwu; Li Shaoying, prefect of Beizhou; Li Shaoqian, defense commissioner of Qizhou; Li Shaoqi, military governor of Heyang; and Li Shaoneng, prefect of Mingzhou—each asked to resume his original name as Huo Yanwei, Chang Congjian, Fang Zhiwen, Wang Yanqiu, Xia Luqi, and Mi Junli—and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaozhen of Wuning, Li Shaoqiong of Zhongwu, Li Shaoying of Beizhou, Li Shaoqian of Qizhou, Li Shaoqi of Heyang, and Li Shaoneng of Mingzhou each asked to restore his original name—Huo Yanwei, Chang Congjian, Fang Zhiwen, Wang Yanqiu, Xia Luqi, and Mi Junli—and the emperor granted their requests.

sentences.zh: 從簡，陳州人也。

translations.literal: Congjian was a man of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian was from Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 晏球本王氏子，畜於杜氏，故請複姓王。

translations.literal: Yanqiu was originally a son of the Wang clan, raised in the Du household, and therefore asked to resume the surname Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiu was originally a Wang by birth but had been raised in the Du household, and therefore asked to restore the surname Wang.

sentences.zh: 丁已，初令百官正衙常朝外，五日一赴內殿起居。

translations.literal: On the day dingji, for the first time the officials, besides regular court at the main hall, were ordered to attend inner-audience greetings once every five days.
translations.idiomatic: On dingji day the emperor for the first time required officials, in addition to regular court, to attend inner-audience greetings every five days.

sentences.zh: 宦官數百人竄匿山林，或落髮為僧，至晉陽者七十餘人，詔北都指揮使李從溫悉誅之。

translations.literal: Several hundred eunuchs fled into hiding in the mountains and forests; some shaved their heads and became monks. More than seventy who reached Taiyuan were ordered by edict to be entirely executed by Li Congwen, commander of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred eunuchs fled into the hills; some shaved their heads and became monks. More than seventy who reached Taiyuan were ordered executed by Li Congwen, commander of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 從溫，帝之侄也。

translations.literal: Congwen was the emperor's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Congwen was the emperor's nephew.

sentences.zh: 帝以前相州刺史安金全有功於晉陽，壬戌，以金全為振武節度使、同平章事。

translations.literal: Because An Jinquan, former prefect of Xiangzhou, had rendered meritorious service at Taiyuan, on the day renxu he was made military governor of Zhenwu and co-equal chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Because An Jinquan, former prefect of Xiangzhou, had served well at Taiyuan, on renxu day he was made military governor of Zhenwu and co-equal chief minister.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，趙在禮請帝幸鄴都。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, Zhao Zaili asked the emperor to visit Ye Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day Zhao Zaili asked the emperor to visit Ye Capital.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以在禮為義成節度使；

translations.literal: on the day wuchen he appointed Zaili military governor of Yicheng;
translations.idiomatic: on wuchen day he appointed Zaili military governor of Yicheng;

sentences.zh: 辭以軍情未聽，不赴鎮。

translations.literal: Zaili declined on the grounds that army sentiment had not yet subsided and did not go to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Zaili declined, saying the troops were still unsettled, and did not take up his post.

sentences.zh: 李彥超入朝，帝曰：「河東無虞，爾之力也。

translations.literal: Li Yanchao entered court. The emperor said, "That Hedong was untroubled is thanks to your efforts.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanchao came to court. The emperor said, "That Hedong remained secure is your doing.

sentences.zh: 」庚午，以為建雄留後。

translations.literal: " On the day gengwu he was made acting prefect of Jianxiong.
translations.idiomatic: " On gengwu day he was appointed acting prefect of Jianxiong.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，加王延翰同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu, Wang Yanhan was given the additional title of co-equal chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day Wang Yanhan was made co-equal chief minister.

sentences.zh: 帝目不知書，四方奏事皆令安重誨讀之，重誨亦不能盡通，乃奏稱：「臣徒以忠實之心事陛下，得典樞機，今事粗能曉知，至於古事，非臣所及。

translations.literal: The emperor's eyes could not read writing; memorials from all quarters were all ordered read by An Chonghui. Chonghui also could not master them all, and therefore memorialized, saying, "Your servant serves Your Majesty only with a loyal and faithful heart and has come to hold the keys of state. I can now roughly understand current affairs, but matters of antiquity are beyond me.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not read; memorials from every quarter were read to him by An Chonghui, who could not master them all either. He therefore memorialized: "I serve Your Majesty only with a loyal heart and now hold the keys of state. I can roughly grasp current affairs, but antiquity is beyond me.

sentences.zh: 願仿前朝侍講、侍讀、近代直崇政、樞密院，選文學之臣與之共事，以備應對。

translations.literal: I beg to follow the former court lecture and reading posts and the recent direct service at Chongzheng and the Palace Secretariat, selecting literary officials to work with me in preparation for responses.
translations.idiomatic: I beg to follow the precedent of lecture and reading posts at court and recent service at Chongzheng and the Palace Secretariat, and to select literary officials to assist me in answering Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」乃置端明殿學士，乙亥，以翰林學士馮道、趙鳳為之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the office of academician of the Duanming Hall was established; on the day yihai the Hanlin academicians Feng Dao and Zhao Feng were appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: " The office of Duanming Hall academician was then established; on yihai day the Hanlin academicians Feng Dao and Zhao Feng were appointed.

sentences.zh: 丙子，聽郭崇韜歸葬，復朱友謙宮爵；

translations.literal: On the day bingzi permission was granted for Guo Chongtao to be returned for burial, and Zhu Youqian's titles and offices were restored;
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day the emperor permitted Guo Chongtao to be returned home for burial and restored Zhu Youqian's titles and offices;

sentences.zh: 兩家貨財田宅，前籍沒者皆歸之。

translations.literal: the goods, wealth, fields, and houses of both families that had previously been confiscated were all returned.
translations.idiomatic: and all goods, lands, and houses previously confiscated from both families were returned.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以安重誨領山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin, An Chonghui was made concurrent military governor of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day An Chonghui was made concurrent military governor of Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 重誨以襄陽要地，不可乏帥，無宜兼領，固辭；

translations.literal: Chonghui, because Xiangyang was a vital place that could not lack a commander, held that it was unsuitable to hold concurrently and firmly declined;
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui argued that Xiangyang was too important to leave without a commander and firmly declined the concurrent appointment;

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔發汴州控鶴指揮使張諫等三千人戍瓦橋。

translations.literal: An edict ordered three thousand men under Zhang Jian, commander of the Crane-Controlled Guard of Bianzhou, and others to garrison Waqiao.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Zhang Jian, commander of the Crane-Controlled Guard of Bianzhou, and three thousand men to garrison Waqiao.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁酉，出城，復還，作亂，焚掠坊市，殺權知州、推官高逖。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day dingyou, they left the city, then returned, rose in mutiny, burned and plundered the wards and markets, and killed Gao Ti, acting prefect and legal officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dingyou day, they marched out of the city, then turned back, mutinied, burned and looted the markets, and killed Gao Ti, acting prefect and legal officer.

sentences.zh: 逼馬步都指揮使、曹州刺史李彥饒為帥，彥饒曰：「汝欲吾為帥，當用吾命，禁止焚掠。

translations.literal: They forced Li Yanrao, commander of horse and foot and prefect of Caozhou, to be their leader. Yanrao said, "If you want me as leader, you must obey my orders and forbid burning and plundering.
translations.idiomatic: They forced Li Yanrao, commander of horse and foot and prefect of Caozhou, to lead them. Yanrao said, "If you want me as your leader, you must obey my orders and stop the burning and looting.

sentences.zh: 」眾從之。

translations.literal: " The crowd obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: " The troops agreed.

sentences.zh: 己亥旦，彥饒伏甲於室，諸將入賀，彥饒曰：「前日唱亂者數人而已。

translations.literal: At dawn on the day jihai, Yanrao hid armed men in the room. When the generals entered to congratulate him, Yanrao said, "Those who stirred up trouble the other day were only a few men.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on jihai day Yanrao hid armed men in the room. When the generals came to congratulate him, he said, "Only a handful of men started the trouble the other day.

sentences.zh: 」遂執張諫等四人，斬之。

translations.literal: " He then seized Zhang Jian and four others and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: " He then seized Zhang Jian and three others and beheaded them.

sentences.zh: 其黨張審瓊帥眾大噪於建國門，彥饒勒兵擊之，盡誅其眾四百人，軍、州始定。

translations.literal: Their partisan Zhang Shenqiong led the crowd in a great uproar at the Jianguo Gate. Yanrao led troops to strike them and executed all four hundred of their followers; the army and prefecture were at last settled.
translations.idiomatic: Their leader Zhang Shenqiong raised a clamor at the Jianguo Gate. Yanrao led troops against them and killed all four hundred mutineers; the army and prefecture were finally pacified.

sentences.zh: 即日，以軍、州事牒節度推官韋儼權知，具以狀聞。

translations.literal: That same day he entrusted military and prefectural affairs to Wei Yan, legal officer of the circuit, as acting administrator, and reported the full circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he entrusted military and prefectural affairs to Wei Yan, the circuit legal officer, as acting administrator and reported the full account to the court.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔以樞密使孔循知汴州，收為亂者三千家，悉誅之。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi an edict appointed Kong Xun, chief palace secretary, to administer Bianzhou; three thousand households implicated in the mutiny were seized and all executed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day an edict appointed Kong Xun, chief palace secretary, to administer Bianzhou. Three thousand households implicated in the mutiny were seized and executed.

sentences.zh: 彥饒，彥超之弟也。

translations.literal: Yanrao was Yanchao's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yanrao was the younger brother of Yanchao.

sentences.zh: 蜀百官至洛陽，永平節度使兼侍中馬全曰：「國亡至此，生不如死！

translations.literal: The hundred officials of Shu reached Luoyang. Ma Quan, military governor of Yongping and concurrent palace attendant, said, "The state has perished to this point—life is not as good as death!
translations.idiomatic: The Shu officials reached Luoyang. Ma Quan, military governor of Yongping and palace attendant, said, "Our state is destroyed—life is worse than death!

sentences.zh: 」不食而卒。

translations.literal: " He ate nothing and died.
translations.idiomatic: " He refused food and died.

sentences.zh: 以平章事王鍇等為諸州府刺史、少尹、判官、司馬，亦有復歸蜀者。

translations.literal: Wang Kai and other chief ministers were appointed prefects, junior administrators, legal officers, and aides of various prefectures; some also returned to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kai and other chief ministers were appointed to posts as prefects, junior administrators, legal officers, and aides in various prefectures; some returned to Shu.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，滑州都指揮使於可洪等縱火作亂，攻魏博戍兵三指揮，逐出之。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, Yu Kehong, commander of Huazhou, and others set fires and rose in mutiny, attacked the three commands of Weibo garrison troops, and drove them out.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day Yu Kehong, commander of Huazhou, and others set fires and mutinied, attacked three Weibo garrison commands, and drove them out.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，敕：「朕二名，但不連稱，皆無所避。

translations.literal: On the day yisi an edict stated: "Our two personal names need not be avoided unless used together in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day an edict stated: "Our two personal names need not be avoided unless used together in sequence.

sentences.zh: 戊申，加西川節度使孟知祥兼侍中。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, Meng Zhixiang, military governor of Xichuan, was given the additional title of palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day Meng Zhixiang, military governor of Xichuan, was made concurrent palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 李繼曮至華州，聞洛中亂，復歸鳳翔；

translations.literal: Li Jiyao reached Huazhou; hearing of the disorder in Luoyang, he returned to Fengxiang;
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiyao reached Huazhou, but when he heard of the chaos in Luoyang he turned back to Fengxiang;

sentences.zh: 帝為之誅柴重厚。

translations.literal: for this the emperor had Chai Zhonghou executed.
translations.idiomatic: for which the emperor had Chai Zhonghou executed.

sentences.zh: 高季興表求夔、忠、萬三州為屬郡，詔許之。

translations.literal: Gao Jixing memorialized requesting that the three prefectures of Kui, Zhong, and Wan be made his subordinate districts; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jixing memorialized asking that Kui, Zhong, and Wan be made his subordinate prefectures; the emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 安重誨恃恩驕橫，殿直馬延誤衝前導，斬之於馬前，御史大夫李琪以聞。

translations.literal: An Chonghui relied on favor and was arrogant and overbearing. The palace attendant Ma Yan, having mistakenly rushed the vanguard, was beheaded before his horse; Chief Censor Li Qi reported it.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui, relying on imperial favor, grew arrogant. When the palace attendant Ma Yan accidentally rushed ahead of his escort, Chonghui beheaded him before his horse. Chief Censor Li Qi reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，重誨白帝下詔，稱延陵突重臣，戒諭中外。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Chonghui had the emperor issue an edict stating that Yan had rudely confronted a great minister and admonishing all within and without.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Chonghui had the emperor issue an edict declaring that Yan had rudely confronted a great minister and warning the court and the realm.

sentences.zh: 於可洪與魏博戍將互相奏雲作亂，帝遣使按驗得實，辛酉，斬可洪於都市，其首謀滑州左崇牙全營族誅，助亂者右崇牙兩長劍建平將校百人亦族誅。

translations.literal: Yu Kehong and the Weibo garrison generals each memorialized accusing the other of raising mutiny. The emperor sent envoys to investigate and verify the facts. On the day xinyou, Kehong was beheaded in the market; the chief plotters, the entire camp of the Left Chongya of Huazhou, were executed to the last clan, and the hundred officers of the Right Chongya who had aided the mutiny were also executed to the last clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kehong and the Weibo garrison generals each accused the other of mutiny. The emperor sent envoys to investigate and found Kehong guilty. On xinyou day Kehong was beheaded in the market. The chief plotters—the entire Left Chongya camp of Huazhou—were executed to the last clan, and the hundred officers of the Right Chongya who had joined the mutiny were likewise exterminated.

sentences.zh: 壬申，初令百官每五日起居，轉對奏事。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, for the first time the officials were ordered to attend greetings every five days and present matters in rotating audience.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day the emperor for the first time required officials to attend greetings every five days and present business in rotating audience.

sentences.zh: 契丹主攻勃海，拔其夫餘城，更命曰東丹國。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler attacked Bohai, captured its Fuyu city, and renamed it the state of Eastern Dan.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler attacked Bohai, captured Fuyu city, and renamed the realm Eastern Dan.

sentences.zh: 命其長子突欲鎮東丹，號人皇王，以次子德光守西樓，號元帥太子。

translations.literal: He appointed his eldest son Tuyu to govern Eastern Dan with the title Human Emperor King, and his second son Deguang to guard the Western Tower with the title Marshal Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed his eldest son Tuyu to govern Eastern Dan as Human Emperor King and his second son Deguang to guard the Western Tower as Marshal Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 帝遣供奉官姚坤告哀於契丹。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the palace attendant Yao Kun to announce the mourning to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the palace attendant Yao Kun to announce Zhuangzong's death to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 契丹主聞莊宗為亂兵所害，慟哭曰：「我朝定兒也。

translations.literal: When the Khitan ruler heard that Zhuangzong had been killed by mutinous soldiers, he wailed and said, "He was my dynasty's sworn son.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan ruler heard that mutineers had killed Zhuangzong, he wept and said, "He was my sworn son.

sentences.zh: 吾方欲救之，以勃海未下，不果往，致吾兒及此。

translations.literal: I was just about to go to save him, but because Bohai was not yet subdued I could not go, and this brought my son to this end.
translations.idiomatic: I was about to go to his aid, but Bohai was not yet subdued and I could not go—so my son came to this end.

sentences.zh: 」哭不已。

translations.literal: " He wept without cease.
translations.idiomatic: " He wept without stopping.

sentences.zh: 虜言「朝定」，猶華言朋友也。

translations.literal: In Khitan speech "dynasty sworn" is like the Chinese word for friend.
translations.idiomatic: In Khitan, "dynasty sworn" means the same as "friend" in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 又謂坤曰：「今天子聞洛陽有急，何不救？

translations.literal: He also said to Kun, "When the Son of Heaven heard that Luoyang was in peril, why did he not rescue it?
translations.idiomatic: He also asked Kun, "When the Son of Heaven heard that Luoyang was in danger, why did he not go to its aid?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「地遠不能及。

translations.literal: " The reply was, "The distance was too great to reach in time.
translations.idiomatic: " Kun answered, "The distance was too great to reach in time.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「何故自立？

translations.literal: " He said, "Why then did he declare himself ruler on his own?
translations.idiomatic: " He asked, "Why then did he declare himself emperor?

sentences.zh: 」坤為言帝所以即位之由，契丹主曰：「漢兒喜飾說，毋多談！

translations.literal: " Kun explained the reasons for the emperor's accession. The Khitan ruler said, "Han people love fine words—say no more!
translations.idiomatic: " Kun explained why the new emperor had taken the throne. The Khitan ruler said, "Han people love fine speeches—enough!

sentences.zh: 」突欲侍側，曰：「牽牛以蹊人之田，而奪之牛，可乎？

translations.literal: " Tuyu, attending at his side, said, "If one leads an ox across another man's field and then seizes the ox—is that permissible?
translations.idiomatic: " Tuyu, standing at his father's side, said, "If someone leads an ox across another man's field and then seizes the ox—is that permissible?

sentences.zh: 」坤曰：「中國無主，唐天子不得已而立；

translations.literal: " Kun said, "The Central Realm had no ruler; the Tang Son of Heaven had no choice but to ascend the throne;
translations.idiomatic: " Kun said, "The Central Realm had no ruler; the Tang emperor had no choice but to ascend the throne;

sentences.zh: 亦由天皇王初有國，豈強取之乎！

translations.literal: it is also like when the Heavenly Emperor King first had a state—did he seize it by force!
translations.idiomatic: just as when the Heavenly Emperor King first established his state—did he seize it by force!

sentences.zh: 」契丹主曰：「理當然。

translations.literal: " The Khitan ruler said, "That is only reasonable.
translations.idiomatic: " The Khitan ruler said, "That is only reasonable.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「聞吾兒專好聲色游畋，不恤軍民，宜其及此。

translations.literal: " He also said, "I hear my son devoted himself only to music, women, hunting, and sport and cared nothing for soldiers and civilians—it was fitting that he came to this.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "I hear my son cared only for music, women, hunting, and sport and neglected soldiers and civilians—it was fitting that he came to this end.

sentences.zh: 我自聞之，舉家不飲酒，散遣伶人，解縱鷹犬。

translations.literal: When I heard of it myself, my whole household stopped drinking wine, dismissed the entertainers, and released the hawks and dogs.
translations.idiomatic: When I heard of it, my whole household stopped drinking, dismissed the entertainers, and released the hawks and dogs.

sentences.zh: 若亦效吾兒所為，行自亡矣。

translations.literal: If you also imitate what my son did, you will soon perish of yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: If you imitate what my son did, you will soon destroy yourselves.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「吾兒與我雖世舊，然屢與我戰急，於今天子則無怨，足以修好。

translations.literal: " He also said, "My son and I, though old friends by generation, fought fiercely many times; toward today's Son of Heaven there is no grudge, and friendship can be restored.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "My son and I were old friends by generation, yet we fought bitterly many times. Toward the present Son of Heaven I bear no grudge, and friendship can be restored.

sentences.zh: 若與我大河之北，吾不復南侵矣。

translations.literal: If you give me the lands north of the Great River, I will no longer invade to the south.
translations.idiomatic: Give me the lands north of the Great River, and I will invade no farther south.

sentences.zh: 」坤曰：「此非使臣之所得專也。

translations.literal: " Kun said, "This is not something your envoy may decide on his own.
translations.idiomatic: " Kun said, "That is not for an envoy to decide on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 」契丹主怒，囚之，旬餘，復召之，曰：「河北恐難得，得鎮、定、幽州亦可也。

translations.literal: " The Khitan ruler was angry and imprisoned him. After more than ten days he summoned him again and said, "Hebei may be hard to obtain; if I can have Zhen, Ding, and You prefectures, that will also do.
translations.idiomatic: " The Khitan ruler was angry and imprisoned him. After more than ten days he summoned him again and said, "Hebei may be impossible to obtain—but Zhen, Ding, and You would suffice.

sentences.zh: 」給紙筆趣令為狀，坤不可，欲殺之，韓延徽諫，乃復囚之。

translations.literal: " He gave him paper and brush and pressed him to write a memorial of agreement. Kun refused; the ruler wished to kill him, but Han Yanhui remonstrated, and he was imprisoned again.
translations.idiomatic: " He gave him paper and brush and pressed him to write a formal pledge. Kun refused. The ruler wished to kill him, but Han Yanhui dissuaded him, and Kun was imprisoned again.

sentences.zh: 丙子，葬光聖神閔孝皇帝於雍陵，廟號莊宗。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi the Sagely, Luminous, Divine, and Compassionate Filial Emperor was buried at Yongling; his temple name was Zhuangzong.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day the Sagely, Luminous, Divine, and Compassionate Filial Emperor was buried at Yongling with the temple name Zhuangzong.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，鎮州留後王建立奏涿州剌史劉殷肇不受代，謀作亂，已討擒之。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, Wang Jianli, acting prefect of Zhenzhou, memorialized that Liu Yinzhao, prefect of Zhuozhou, had refused to yield his post, plotted rebellion, and had already been attacked and captured.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day Wang Jianli, acting prefect of Zhenzhou, reported that Liu Yinzhao, prefect of Zhuozhou, had refused to yield his post, plotted rebellion, and had been captured.

sentences.zh: 己卯，置彰國軍於應州。

translations.literal: On the day jimao the Zhangguo Army was established at Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day the Zhangguo Army was established at Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎、同平章事豆盧革、韋說奏事帝前，或時禮貌不盡恭；

translations.literal: Doulu Ge and Wei Shuo, vice grand councilors of the Chancellery and co-equal chief ministers, when presenting business before the emperor sometimes showed courtesy that was not fully respectful;
translations.idiomatic: Doulu Ge and Wei Shuo, vice grand councilors and co-equal chief ministers, sometimes showed less than full respect when presenting business to the emperor;

sentences.zh: 百官俸錢皆折估，而革父子獨受實錢；

translations.literal: the salary money of all officials was discounted in valuation, but Ge and his son alone received cash in full;
translations.idiomatic: all officials' salaries were paid at a discounted valuation, but Ge and his son alone received cash in full;

sentences.zh: 百官自五月給，而革父子自正月給；

translations.literal: all officials were paid from the fifth month, but Ge and his son from the first month;
translations.idiomatic: all officials were paid from the fifth month, but Ge and his son from the first;

sentences.zh: 由是眾論沸騰。

translations.literal: for this public opinion seethed.
translations.idiomatic: public opinion seethed against them.

sentences.zh: 說以孫為子，奏官；

translations.literal: Shuo presented his grandson as his son and memorialized for an office for him;
translations.idiomatic: Shuo presented his grandson as his son and memorialized for an office;

sentences.zh: 受選人王參賂，除近官。

translations.literal: he accepted a bribe from the candidate Wang Can and appointed him to a nearby office.
translations.idiomatic: he accepted a bribe from the candidate Wang Can and appointed him to a nearby post.

sentences.zh: 中旨以庫部郎中蕭希甫為諫議大夫，革、說覆奏。

translations.literal: An imperial order appointed Xiao Xifu, director in the treasury department, remonstrance grandee; Ge and Shuo submitted a counter-memorial.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order appointed Xiao Xifu, director in the treasury department, remonstrance grandee; Ge and Shuo submitted a counter-memorial.

sentences.zh: 希甫恨之，上疏言「革、說不忠前朝，阿庚取容」；

translations.literal: Xifu resented this and memorialized that "Ge and Shuo were disloyal to the former dynasty and fawned on the new to win favor";
translations.idiomatic: Xifu resented this and memorialized that Ge and Shuo had been disloyal to the former dynasty and fawned on the new regime;

sentences.zh: 因誣「革強奪民田，縱田客殺人；

translations.literal: he further falsely charged that "Ge forcibly seized commoners' fields and allowed his tenant farmers to kill people;
translations.idiomatic: he further charged that Ge had forcibly seized commoners' fields and allowed his tenant farmers to kill people;

sentences.zh: 說奪鄰家井，取宿藏物。

translations.literal: Shuo seized a neighbor's well and took stored goods.
translations.idiomatic: and that Shuo had seized a neighbor's well and taken stored goods.

sentences.zh: 」制貶革辰州刺史，說漵州剌史。

translations.literal: " An edict demoted Ge to prefect of Chenzhou and Shuo to prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict demoted Ge to prefect of Chenzhou and Shuo to prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，賜希甫金帛，擢為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, Xifu was given gold and silks and promoted to attendant cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day Xifu was rewarded with gold and silks and promoted to attendant cavalier.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，契丹主阿保機卒於夫餘城，述律-{后}-召諸將及酋長難制者之妻，謂曰：「我今寡居，汝不可不效我。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, the Khitan ruler Abaoji died at Fuyu city. Empress Shulü summoned the wives of generals and chieftains who were hard to control and said, "I am now a widow—you cannot fail to follow my example.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day the Khitan ruler Abaoji died at Fuyu city. Empress Shulü summoned the wives of generals and chieftains who were hard to control and said, "I am now a widow—you must follow my example.

sentences.zh: 」又集其夫泣問曰：「汝思先帝乎？

translations.literal: " She then gathered their husbands, wept, and asked, "Do you miss the late emperor?
translations.idiomatic: " She then gathered their husbands, wept, and asked, "Do you miss the late emperor?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「受先帝恩，豈得不思！

translations.literal: " The reply was, "Having received the late emperor's grace, how could we not miss him!
translations.idiomatic: " They answered, "Having received the late emperor's grace, how could we not miss him!

sentences.zh: 」曰：「果思之，宜往見之。

translations.literal: " She said, "If you truly miss him, you should go to see him.
translations.idiomatic: " She said, "If you truly miss him, you should go join him.

sentences.zh: 」遂殺之。

translations.literal: " She then had them killed.
translations.idiomatic: " She then had them killed.

sentences.zh: 癸未，再貶豆盧革費州司戶，韋說夷州司戶。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei, Ge was demoted again to registrar of Feizhou and Shuo to registrar of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day Ge was demoted again to registrar of Feizhou and Shuo to registrar of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 甲申，革流陵州，說流合州。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, Ge was exiled to Lingzhou and Shuo to Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day Ge was exiled to Lingzhou and Shuo to Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥陰有據蜀之志，閱庫中，得鎧甲二十萬，置左右牙等兵十六營，凡萬六千人，營於牙城內外。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang secretly harbored the ambition to hold Shu. Inspecting the storehouses, he found two hundred thousand suits of armor and established sixteen camps of left and right guard troops and the like, altogether sixteen thousand men, encamped inside and outside the headquarters city.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang secretly intended to hold Shu. Inspecting the storehouses he found two hundred thousand suits of armor and established sixteen camps of guard troops, sixteen thousand men in all, encamped inside and outside headquarters.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙酉朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the first day of the month (yiyou), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the first day, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，契丹述律-{后}-使少子安端少君守東丹，與長子突欲奉契丹主之喪，將其眾發夫餘城。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, Khitan Empress Shulü had her youngest son Anduan Shaojun guard Eastern Dan and, with her eldest son Tuyu, escorted the Khitan ruler's coffin and led their followers out from Fuyu city.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day Empress Shulü left her youngest son Anduan to guard Eastern Dan and, with her eldest son Tuyu, escorted the Khitan ruler's coffin and led their followers out from Fuyu city.

sentences.zh: 初，郭崇韜以蜀騎兵分左、右驍衛等六營，凡三千人；

translations.literal: Earlier, Guo Chongtao had divided the Shu cavalry into six camps such as the left and right Swift Guard, altogether three thousand men;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Guo Chongtao had organized the Shu cavalry into six camps including the left and right Swift Guard, three thousand men in all;

sentences.zh: 步兵分左、右寧遠等二十營，凡二萬四千人。

translations.literal: the infantry were divided into twenty camps such as the left and right Tranquil Distance, altogether twenty-four thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: and the infantry into twenty camps including the left and right Tranquil Distance, twenty-four thousand men in all.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，孟知祥增置左、右衝山等六營，凡六千人，營於羅城內外；

translations.literal: On the day gengyin, Meng Zhixiang added six camps such as the left and right Mountain Assault, altogether six thousand men, encamped inside and outside the outer wall;
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day Meng Zhixiang added six camps including the left and right Mountain Assault, six thousand men, encamped inside and outside the outer wall;

sentences.zh: 又置義寧等二十營，凡萬六千人，分戍管內州縣就食；

translations.literal: he also established twenty camps such as Righteous Peace, altogether sixteen thousand men, dispersed to garrison prefectures and counties within his circuit for local provisioning;
translations.idiomatic: he also established twenty camps including Righteous Peace, sixteen thousand men, dispersed to garrison prefectures and counties within his circuit for local provisioning;

sentences.zh: 又置左、右牢城四營，凡四千人，分戍成都境內。

translations.literal: he further established four camps of left and right Walled City, altogether four thousand men, dispersed to garrison within the Chengdu region.
translations.idiomatic: and four Walled City camps, four thousand men, garrisoned within the Chengdu region.

sentences.zh: 王公儼既殺楊希望，欲邀節鉞，揚言符習為治嚴急，軍府眾情不願其還。

translations.literal: After Wang Gongyi had killed Yang Xiwang, he wished to obtain the military commission and spread word that Fu Xi's governance was harsh and severe and that the army and prefectural staff did not wish him to return.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Gongyi killed Yang Xiwang, he sought the military commission and spread word that Fu Xi's governance was harsh and that the army and prefectural staff did not want him back.

sentences.zh: 習還，至齊州，公儼拒之，習不改前。

translations.literal: When Xi returned and reached Qizhou, Gongyi refused him entry; Xi did not alter his former conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi returned to Qizhou, Gongyi refused him entry, but Xi did not alter his conduct.

sentences.zh: 公儼又令將士上表請己為帥，詔除登州剌史。

translations.literal: Gongyi again had his officers and soldiers submit a memorial asking that he be made commander; an edict appointed him prefect of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi had his officers submit a memorial asking that he be made commander; the court appointed him prefect of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 公儼不時之官，托雲軍情所留，帝乃徙天平節度使霍彥威為平盧節度使，聚兵淄州，以圖攻取，公儼懼，乙未，始之官。

translations.literal: Gongyi did not promptly take up his post, pleading that army sentiment kept him there. The emperor then transferred Huo Yanwei, military governor of Tianping, to be military governor of Pinglu, gathered troops at Zizhou to plan an attack, and Gongyi, in fear, on the day yiwei at last went to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi did not promptly take up his post, claiming the troops kept him there. The emperor transferred Huo Yanwei from Tianping to Pinglu and gathered troops at Zizhou to attack him. Gongyi, in fear, at last went to his post on yiwei day.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，彥威至青州，追擒之，並其族黨悉斬之，支使北海韓叔嗣預焉。
