translations.literal: On the day dingyou, Yanwei reached Qingzhou, pursued and captured him, and beheaded him together with all his kinsmen and partisans; Han Shusi of Beihai, the circuit aide, was among them.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day Yanwei reached Qingzhou, pursued and captured Gongyi, and beheaded him with all his kinsmen and partisans, including Han Shusi of Beihai, the circuit aide.

sentences.zh: 其子熙載將奔吳，密告其友汝陰進士李穀，穀送至正陽，痛飲而別。

translations.literal: His son Xizai was about to flee to Wu and secretly told his friend Li Gu, a jinshi of Ruyin; Gu escorted him to Zhengyang, and they drank heavily in parting.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xizai planned to flee to Wu and secretly told his friend Li Gu, a jinshi of Ruyin. Gu escorted him to Zhengyang, where they drank heavily in parting.

sentences.zh: 熙載謂穀曰：「吳若用吾為相，當長驅以定中原。

translations.literal: Xizai said to Gu, "If Wu employs me as chief minister, I shall drive straight through and pacify the Central Plain.
translations.idiomatic: Xizai told Gu, "If Wu makes me chief minister, I shall drive straight north and pacify the Central Plain.

sentences.zh: 」穀笑曰：「中原若用吾為相，取吳如囊中物耳。

translations.literal: " Gu laughed and said, "If the Central Plain employs me as chief minister, taking Wu will be like picking something from a bag.
translations.idiomatic: " Gu laughed and said, "If the Central Plain makes me chief minister, taking Wu will be like picking something from a bag.

sentences.zh: 庚子，幽州言契丹寇邊，命齊州防禦使安審通將兵御之。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, Youzhou reported that the Khitan were raiding the border; An Shentong, defense commissioner of Qizhou, was ordered to lead troops to repel them.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day Youzhou reported Khitan border raids; An Shentong, defense commissioner of Qizhou, was ordered to lead troops against them.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬戌，孟知祥置左、右飛棹兵六營，凡六千人，分戍濱江諸州，習水戰以備夔、峽。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day renxu, Meng Zhixiang established six camps of left and right Flying Oar troops, altogether six thousand men, dispersed to garrison prefectures along the river, practicing naval warfare to prepare against Kui and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renxu day, Meng Zhixiang established six camps of Flying Oar troops, six thousand men, garrisoned along the river to train for naval warfare against Kui and Xia.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，盧龍節度使李紹斌請複姓趙，從之，仍賜名德鈞。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, Li Shaobin, military governor of Lulong, asked to resume the surname Zhao; permission was granted, and he was further given the name Dejun.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day Li Shaobin, military governor of Lulong, asked to restore the surname Zhao; the emperor agreed and gave him the name Dejun.

sentences.zh: 德鈞養子延壽尚帝女興平公主，故德鈞成蒙親任。

translations.literal: Dejun's adopted son Yanshou had married the emperor's daughter Princess Xingping; therefore Dejun came to enjoy intimate trust.
translations.idiomatic: Dejun's adopted son Yanshou had married the emperor's daughter Princess Xingping, and Dejun thereby won the emperor's intimate trust.

sentences.zh: 延壽本蓨令劉邟之子也。

translations.literal: Yanshou was originally the son of Liu Xing, magistrate of Tiao.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou was originally the son of Liu Xing, magistrate of Tiao.

sentences.zh: 加楚王殷守尚書令。

translations.literal: Prince Chu Yin Shou was given the additional title of director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chu Yin Shou was made concurrent director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 契丹述律-{后}-愛中子德光，欲立之，至西樓，命與突欲俱乘馬立帳前，謂諸奠長曰：「二子吾皆愛之，莫知所立，汝曹擇可立者執其轡。

translations.literal: Khitan Empress Shulü loved her middle son Deguang and wished to install him. When they reached the Western Tower, she ordered him and Tuyu to mount horses and stand before the tent, and said to the various chieftains, "I love both sons and do not know whom to install—you choose the one fit to rule and take his bridle.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Shulü loved her middle son Deguang and wished to make him ruler. At the Western Tower she had him and Tuyu mount horses and stand before the tent, and told the chieftains, "I love both sons and cannot choose—take the bridle of the one fit to rule.

sentences.zh: 」酋長知其意，爭執德光轡歡躍曰：「願事元帥太子。

translations.literal: " The chieftains knew her intent, vied to seize Deguang's bridle, and leaped for joy, saying, "We wish to serve the Marshal Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: " The chieftains understood her intent, seized Deguang's bridle, and leaped for joy: "We wish to serve the Marshal Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 」後曰：「眾之所欲，吾安敢違？

translations.literal: " The empress said, "What the multitude desires—how dare I oppose it?
translations.idiomatic: " The empress said, "What the multitude desires—how dare I oppose it?

sentences.zh: 」遂立之為天皇王，突欲慍，帥數百騎欲奔唐，為邏者所遏；

translations.literal: " He was thereupon installed as Heavenly Emperor King. Tuyu was resentful and led several hundred horsemen wishing to flee to Tang, but was stopped by patrols;
translations.idiomatic: " Deguang was installed as Heavenly Emperor King. Tuyu, resentful, led several hundred horsemen intending to flee to Tang but was stopped by patrols;

sentences.zh: 述律-{后}-不罪，遣歸東丹。

translations.literal: Empress Shulü did not punish him and sent him back to Eastern Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Shulü did not punish him and sent him back to Eastern Dan.

sentences.zh: 天皇王尊述律-{后}-為太后，國事皆決焉。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Emperor King honored Empress Shulü as empress dowager, and all state affairs were decided by her.
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Emperor King honored Empress Shulü as empress dowager, and she decided all state affairs.

sentences.zh: 太后復納其侄為天皇王后。

translations.literal: The empress dowager again took her nephew as consort to the Heavenly Emperor King.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager took her nephew as consort to the Heavenly Emperor King.

sentences.zh: 天皇王性孝謹，母病不食亦不食，侍於母前應對或不稱旨，母揚眉視之，輒懼而趨避，非復召不敢見也。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Emperor King was filial and cautious by nature; when his mother was ill he ate nothing either, and when attending before her, if his replies sometimes did not suit her intent and she raised her brows to look at him, he would at once fearfully hurry away and would not dare appear again unless summoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Emperor King was filial and cautious. When his mother was ill he ate nothing. If his replies before her did not please her and she raised her brows, he would flee in fear and would not dare appear again unless summoned.

sentences.zh: 以韓延徽為政事令。

translations.literal: Han Yanhui was made director of government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yanhui was made director of government affairs.

sentences.zh: 聽姚坤歸覆命，遣其臣阿思沒骨餒來告哀。

translations.literal: Yao Kun was permitted to return and report; the Khitan sent their minister Asimugunai to announce the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Kun was permitted to return and report; the Khitan sent their minister Asimugunai to announce the mourning.

sentences.zh: 壬午，賜李繼曮名從曮。

translations.literal: On the day renwu, Li Jiyao was given the name Congyao.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day Li Jiyao was given the name Congyao.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲申朔，初賜文武官春冬衣。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day of the month (jiashen), spring and winter garments were for the first time granted to civil and military officials.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day, spring and winter garments were for the first time granted to civil and military officials.

sentences.zh: 昭武節度使、同平章事王延翰，驕淫殘暴，己丑，自稱大閩國王。

translations.literal: Wang Yanhan, military governor of Zhaowu and co-equal chief minister, was arrogant, licentious, cruel, and violent; on the day jichou he declared himself King of Great Min.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanhan, military governor of Zhaowu and co-equal chief minister, was arrogant, licentious, cruel, and violent; on jichou day he declared himself King of Great Min.

sentences.zh: 立宮殿，置百官，威儀文物皆仿天子之制，群下稱之曰殿下。

translations.literal: He established palaces and offices, and ceremonial regalia and ritual objects all imitated the Son of Heaven's system; his subordinates addressed him as Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: He built palaces, appointed officials, and imitated the Son of Heaven in ceremonial regalia; his subordinates addressed him as Your Highness.

sentences.zh: 赦境內，追尊其父審知曰昭武王。

translations.literal: He proclaimed an amnesty within his borders and posthumously honored his father Shenzhi as King Zhaowu.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed an amnesty and posthumously honored his father Shenzhi as King Zhaowu.

sentences.zh: 靜難節度使毛璋，驕僭不法，訓卒繕兵，有跋扈之志，詔以穎州團練使李承約為節度副使以察之。

translations.literal: Mao Zhang, military governor of Jingnan, was arrogant, overstepping, and lawless; he trained soldiers and repaired weapons and had the ambition of a domineering warlord. An edict appointed Li Chengyue, regimental commander of Yingzhou, military governor deputy to observe him.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Zhang, military governor of Jingnan, was arrogant and lawless; he trained troops and repaired weapons with domineering ambition. The court appointed Li Chengyue, regimental commander of Yingzhou, as his deputy to watch him.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，徙璋為昭義節度使。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, Zhang was transferred to be military governor of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day Zhang was transferred to military governor of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 璋欲不奉詔，承約與觀察判官長安邊蔚從容說諭，久之，乃肯受代。

translations.literal: Zhang wished not to obey the edict; Chengyue and the observation legal officer Bian Wei of Chang'an gently persuaded and instructed him, and after a long while he at last consented to yield his post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang wished to disobey; Chengyue and the observation legal officer Bian Wei of Chang'an gently persuaded him, and after a long while he agreed to yield his post.

sentences.zh: 庚子，幽州奏契丹盧龍節度使盧文時來奔。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, Youzhou memorialized that Lu Wenshi, Khitan military governor of Lulong, had come over in flight.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day Youzhou reported that Lu Wenshi, Khitan military governor of Lulong, had defected.

sentences.zh: 初，文進為契丹守平州，帝即位，遣間使說之，以易代之後，無復嫌怨。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wenjin had guarded Pingzhou for the Khitan. When the emperor acceded, he sent secret envoys to persuade him that after the change of dynasties there would be no further grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wenjin had guarded Pingzhou for the Khitan. When the emperor acceded he sent secret envoys to persuade him that after the change of dynasties old grudges need not remain.

sentences.zh: 文進所部皆華人，思歸，乃殺契丹戍平州者，帥其眾十餘萬、車帳八千乘來奔。

translations.literal: Wenjin's followers were all Chinese who longed to return; he therefore killed the Khitan garrison at Pingzhou and led his followers, more than one hundred thousand men and eight thousand carts and tents, to come over in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin's followers were all Chinese who longed to return. He killed the Khitan garrison at Pingzhou and led more than one hundred thousand men and eight thousand carts and tents in flight to Tang.

sentences.zh: 初，魏王繼岌、郭崇韜率蜀中富民輸犒賞錢五百萬緡，聽以金銀繒帛充，晝夜督責，有自殺者，給軍之餘，猶二百萬緡。

translations.literal: Earlier, Prince of Wei Li Jiji and Guo Chongtao had led the wealthy of Shu to deliver five million strings in reward money, permitting payment in gold, silver, and silks; they pressed day and night, and some killed themselves. After supplying the army, there still remained two million strings.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Prince of Wei Li Jiji and Guo Chongtao had levied five million strings in reward money from the wealthy of Shu, accepting gold, silver, and silks; they pressed day and night until some killed themselves. After supplying the army, two million strings remained.

sentences.zh: 至是，任圜判三司，知成都富饒，遣鹽鐵判官、太僕卿趙季良為孟知祥官告國信兼三川都制置轉運使。

translations.literal: At this time Ren Huan held charge of the three departments, knew that Chengdu was rich, and sent Zhao Jiliang, salt-and-iron commissioner and minister of the stud, as envoy bearing the commission to Meng Zhixiang and concurrent commissioner for transport and provisioning of the Three Gorges region.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Huan, overseeing the three fiscal departments, knew Chengdu was rich and sent Zhao Jiliang, salt-and-iron commissioner and minister of the stud, as envoy to Meng Zhixiang with authority over transport and provisioning in the Three Gorges region.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，季良至成都。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen, Jiliang reached Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day Jiliang reached Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 蜀人欲皆不與，知祥曰：「府庫他人所聚，輸之可也。

translations.literal: The people of Shu wished to give nothing at all. Zhixiang said, "The treasury stores were gathered by others—those may be delivered.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu wished to give nothing. Zhixiang said, "Treasury stores gathered by others may be delivered.

sentences.zh: 州縣租稅，以贍鎮兵十萬，決不可得。

translations.literal: The prefectural and county land taxes, used to support one hundred thousand garrison troops, absolutely cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county land taxes that support one hundred thousand garrison troops are absolutely unavailable.

sentences.zh: 」季良但發庫物，不敢復言制置轉運職事矣。

translations.literal: " Jiliang only released treasury goods and dared speak no more of transport and provisioning duties.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiliang released only treasury goods and dared speak no more of transport and provisioning.

sentences.zh: 安重誨以知祥及東川節度使董璋皆據險要，擁強兵，恐久而難制；

translations.literal: An Chonghui, because Zhixiang and Dong Chuan military governor Dong Zhang both held strategic terrain and commanded strong armies, feared that in time they would be hard to control;
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui feared that Zhixiang and Dong Chuan military governor Dong Zhang, holding strategic terrain and strong armies, would grow hard to control;

sentences.zh: 又知祥乃莊宗近姻，陰欲圖之。

translations.literal: and because Zhixiang was a close in-law of Zhuangzong, secretly wished to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: and because Zhixiang was a close in-law of Zhuangzong, secretly plotted against him.

sentences.zh: 客省使、泗州防禦使李嚴自請為西川監軍，必能制知祥；

translations.literal: Li Yan, commissioner of the Reception Bureau and defense commissioner of Sizhou, volunteered to be military supervisor of Xichuan and said he could certainly control Zhixiang;
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan, commissioner of the Reception Bureau and defense commissioner of Sizhou, volunteered as military supervisor of Xichuan, claiming he could control Zhixiang;

sentences.zh: 己酉，以嚴為西川都監，文思使太原朱弘昭為東川副使。

translations.literal: on the day jiyou he was made military supervisor of Xichuan, and Zhu Hongzhao of Taiyuan, commissioner of literary affairs, was made deputy supervisor of Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: on jiyou day Yan was made military supervisor of Xichuan and Zhu Hongzhao of Taiyuan, commissioner of literary affairs, deputy supervisor of Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 李嚴母賢明，謂嚴曰：「汝前啟滅蜀之謀，今日再往，必以死報蜀人矣。

translations.literal: Li Yan's mother was wise and clear-sighted. She said to Yan, "You earlier proposed the plan to destroy Shu; if you go again today, the people of Shu will surely repay you with death.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan's mother was wise. She told him, "You earlier proposed destroying Shu; if you go again, the people of Shu will surely kill you.

sentences.zh: 舊制，吏部給告身，先責其人輸朱膠綾軸錢。

translations.literal: By old regulation, when the Ministry of Personnel issued commission documents, it first required the recipient to pay money for cinnabar glue and brocade scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: By old regulation the Ministry of Personnel required recipients to pay for cinnabar glue and brocade scrolls before issuing commission documents.

sentences.zh: 喪亂以來，貧者但受敕牒，多不取告身。

translations.literal: Since the disorders, the poor received only edict copies and mostly did not take the formal commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Since the disorders the poor received only edict copies and mostly did not take formal commissions.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲戌，吏部侍郎劉岳上言：「告身有褒貶訓戒之辭，豈可使其人初不之睹！

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day jiaxu, Liu Yue, vice minister of personnel, memorialized, "Commission documents contain words of praise, blame, instruction, and warning—how can we let the recipient never see them at first!
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiaxu day, Liu Yue, vice minister of personnel, memorialized: "Commission documents contain words of praise, blame, instruction, and warning—how can recipients never see them!

sentences.zh: 」敕文班丞、郎、給、諫，武班大將軍以上，宜賜告身。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered that for the civil roster—assistants, court gentlemen, presenters, and remonstrators—and for the military roster of great generals and above, commission documents should be granted.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered commission documents for civil officials from assistants through remonstrators and for military officials of great general rank and above.

sentences.zh: 其後執政議，以為朱膠綾軸，厥費無多，朝廷受以官祿，何惜小費！

translations.literal: Thereafter the chief ministers deliberated and held that cinnabar glue and brocade scrolls cost little; the court received official salaries from them—why spare a small expense!
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers then argued that cinnabar glue and brocade scrolls cost little and that the court received official salaries in return—why spare a small expense!

sentences.zh: 乃奏：「凡除官者更不輸錢，皆賜告身。

translations.literal: They therefore memorialized, "For all appointees, no further payment shall be required; commission documents shall all be granted.
translations.idiomatic: They memorialized that appointees need pay no further fees and that all should receive commission documents.

sentences.zh: 」當是時，所除正員官之外，其餘試銜、帖號止以寵激軍中將校而已，及長興以後，所除浸多，乃至軍中卒伍，使、州、鎮、戍胥史，皆得銀青階及憲官，歲賜告身以萬數矣。

translations.literal: " At that time, besides regular appointees, the rest—probationary titles and posted designations—were only to favor and encourage officers in the army. After the Changxing era appointments gradually increased, until even army rank-and-file, commissioners, prefectures, garrisons, and clerks all obtained silver-green ranks and censorate posts, and commission documents granted yearly reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time probationary titles served only to reward army officers. After the Changxing era appointments multiplied until even rank-and-file soldiers and clerks received silver-green ranks and censorate posts, and tens of thousands of commission documents were granted yearly.

sentences.zh: 閩王延翰蔑棄兄弟，襲位才逾月，出其弟延鈞為泉州刺史。

translations.literal: King Yanhan of Min despised and cast aside his brothers; barely a month after succeeding, he sent out his younger brother Yanjun as prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: King Yanhan of Min despised his brothers; barely a month after succeeding he sent his younger brother Yanjun to Quanzhou as prefect.

sentences.zh: 延翰多取民女以充後庭，采擇不已。

translations.literal: Yanhan took many commoners' daughters to fill his rear apartments and never ceased selecting more.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhan took many commoners' daughters for his harem and never ceased selecting more.

sentences.zh: 延鈞上書極諫，延翰怒，由是有隙。

translations.literal: Yanjun memorialized in strongest remonstrance; Yanhan was angry, and from this a rift arose.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjun memorialized in strong remonstrance; Yanhan was angry, and a rift opened between them.

sentences.zh: 父審知養子延稟為建州刺史，延翰與書使之采擇，延稟覆書不遜，亦有隙。

translations.literal: Their father Shenzhi's adopted son Yanbing was prefect of Jianzhou; Yanhan wrote him ordering selections, and Yanbing's reply was insubordinate—there was a rift there as well.
translations.idiomatic: Their father's adopted son Yanbing was prefect of Jianzhou. Yanhan wrote ordering selections; Yanbing's reply was insubordinate, and they too fell out.

sentences.zh: 十二月，延稟、延鈞合兵襲福州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Yanbing and Yanjun combined forces to attack Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Yanbing and Yanjun combined forces and attacked Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 延稟順流先至，福州指揮使陳陶帥眾拒之，兵敗，陶自殺。

translations.literal: Yanbing went downstream first; Chen Tao, commander of Fuzhou, led troops to resist, was defeated, and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbing went downstream first. Chen Tao, commander of Fuzhou, led troops to resist, was defeated, and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 是夜，延稟帥壯士百餘人趣西門，梯城而入，執守門者，發庫取兵仗。

translations.literal: That night Yanbing led more than a hundred stalwarts to the west gate, scaled the wall and entered, seized the gate guards, and opened the storehouses for weapons.
translations.idiomatic: That night Yanbing led more than a hundred stalwarts to the west gate, scaled the wall, seized the gate guards, and opened the armories.

sentences.zh: 及寢門，延翰驚匿別室；

translations.literal: Reaching the sleeping gate, Yanhan fled in alarm to a side room;
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the sleeping quarters, Yanhan fled in alarm to a side room;

sentences.zh: 辛卯旦，延稟執之，暴其罪惡，且稱延翰與妻崔氏共弒先王，告諭吏民，斬於紫宸門外。

translations.literal: at dawn on the day xinmao Yanbing seized him, exposed his crimes, and declared that Yanhan and his wife the Cui had together murdered the former king; he informed officials and people and beheaded him outside the Zichen Gate.
translations.idiomatic: at dawn on xinmao day Yanbing seized him, exposed his crimes, and declared that Yanhan and his wife Lady Cui had murdered the former king; he informed officials and people and beheaded him outside the Zichen Gate.

sentences.zh: 是日，延鈞至成南，延稟開門納之，推延鈞為威武留後。

translations.literal: That day Yanjun reached the south of the wall; Yanbing opened the gate and admitted him, and Yanjun was installed as acting prefect of Weiwu.
translations.idiomatic: That day Yanjun reached the south wall; Yanbing opened the gate and admitted him, and Yanjun was installed as acting prefect of Weiwu.

sentences.zh: 癸已，以盧文進為義成節度使、同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, Lu Wenjin was made military governor of Yicheng and co-equal chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day Lu Wenjin was appointed military governor of Yicheng and co-equal chief minister.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以皇子從榮為天雄節度使、同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, the imperial prince Congrong was made military governor of Tianxiong and co-equal chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day the imperial prince Congrong was appointed military governor of Tianxiong and co-equal chief minister.

sentences.zh: 趙季良等運蜀金帛十億至洛陽，時朝遷方匱乏，賴此以濟。

translations.literal: Zhao Jiliang and others transported a billion in Shu gold and silks to Luoyang; at that time the court was short of funds and relied on this for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jiliang and others transported a billion in Shu gold and silks to Luoyang. The court was desperately short of funds and was saved by this shipment.

sentences.zh: 是歲，吳越王鏐以中國喪亂，朝命不通，改元寶正；

translations.literal: That year, Qian Liu, King of Wuyue, because of the disorders in the Central Realm and the break in court orders, changed the era name to Baozheng;
translations.idiomatic: That year King Qian Liu of Wuyue, citing disorders in the Central Realm and the break in contact with the court, changed his era name to Baozheng;

sentences.zh: 其後復通中國，乃諱而不稱。

translations.literal: after contact with the Central Realm was restored, he avoided mentioning it.
translations.idiomatic: when contact with the Central Realm was restored, he avoided mentioning it.

sentences.zh: 明宗聖德和武欽孝皇帝上之下天成二年（

translations.literal: Emperor Mingzong, Sagely in Virtue, Harmonious in Martial Prowess, and Reverent in Filial Piety—upper section, lower part; second year of Tiancheng (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong the Sagely, Harmonious, Martial, and Filial—continued; second year of Tiancheng (

sentences.zh: 丁亥，公元九二七年）

translations.literal: dinghai, corresponding to 927 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸丑朔，帝更名亶。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the first day of the month (guichou), the emperor changed his personal name to Dan.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month, the emperor changed his personal name to Dan.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥聞李嚴來監其軍，惡之；

translations.literal: When Meng Zhixiang heard that Li Yan was coming to supervise his army, he hated it;
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Zhixiang heard that Li Yan was coming to supervise his army, he was displeased;

sentences.zh: 或請奏止之，知祥曰：「何必然，吾有以待之。

translations.literal: someone asked to memorialize stopping him. Zhixiang said, "Why be so certain? I have a way to deal with him.
translations.idiomatic: someone asked to memorialize blocking the appointment. Zhixiang said, "Why assume the worst? I have a way to deal with him.

sentences.zh: 」遣吏至綿、劍迎候。

translations.literal: " He sent officials to Mian and Jian to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent officials to Mian and Jian to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 會武信節度使李紹文卒，知祥自言嘗受密詔許便宜從事，壬戌，以西川節度副使、內外馬步軍都指揮使李敬周為遂州留後，趣之上道，然後表聞。

translations.literal: When Li Shaowen, military governor of Wuxin, died, Zhixiang declared that he had once received a secret edict permitting discretionary action. On the day renxu he appointed Li Jingzhou, vice military governor of Xichuan and commander of internal and external horse and foot, acting prefect of Suizhou, urged him on the road, and only then memorialized the court.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shaowen, military governor of Wuxin, died, Zhixiang claimed he had a secret edict allowing discretionary action. On renxu day he appointed Li Jingzhou, his vice military governor and army commander, acting prefect of Suizhou, sent him on his way, and only then informed the court.

sentences.zh: 嚴先遣使至成都，知祥自以於嚴有舊恩，冀其懼而自回，乃盛陳甲兵以示之，嚴不以為意。

translations.literal: Yan first sent an envoy to Chengdu. Zhixiang, thinking he had shown Yan old favor and hoping Yan would fear and turn back on his own, arrayed armor and troops in great display; Yan paid it no mind.
translations.idiomatic: Yan first sent an envoy to Chengdu. Zhixiang, believing he had once favored Yan and hoping Yan would turn back in fear, displayed his troops in full armor; Yan was unmoved.

sentences.zh: 安重誨以孔循少侍宮禁，謂其諳練故事，知朝士行能，多聽其言。

translations.literal: An Chonghui, because Kong Xun had served in the palace precincts from youth, held that he was versed in precedent and knew the conduct and ability of court officials, and often followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui, because Kong Xun had served in the palace from youth, believed him versed in precedent and knowledgeable about court officials, and often followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 豆盧革、韋說既得罪，朝延議置相，循意不欲用河北人，先已薦鄭玨，又薦太常卿崔協。

translations.literal: After Doulu Ge and Wei Shuo had been punished, the court deliberated on appointing chief ministers. Xun did not wish to use men from Hebei; he had already recommended Zheng Jue and now recommended Cui Xie, minister of imperial sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After Ge and Shuo were punished, the court deliberated on new chief ministers. Xun opposed men from Hebei; he had already recommended Zheng Jue and now recommended Cui Xie, minister of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 任圜欲用御史大夫李琪；

translations.literal: Ren Huan wished to use Li Qi, chief censor;
translations.idiomatic: Ren Huan wanted Li Qi, chief censor;

sentences.zh: 鄭玨素惡琪，故循力沮之，謂重誨曰：「李琪非無文學，但不廉耳。

translations.literal: Zheng Jue had always hated Qi, so Xun strongly obstructed him and said to Chonghui, "Li Qi is not without literary learning, but he is not honest.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jue hated Qi, so Xun strongly opposed him and told Chonghui, "Li Qi has learning, but he is not honest.

sentences.zh: 宰相但得端重有器度者，足以儀刑多士矣。

translations.literal: For chief minister one need only have someone dignified and of breadth—that is enough to set an example for the multitude of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: A chief minister need only be dignified and magnanimous—enough to set an example for the court.

sentences.zh: 」它日議於上前，上問誰可相者，重誨以協對。

translations.literal: " Another day they deliberated before the emperor, who asked who could serve as chief minister; Chonghui answered with Xie.
translations.idiomatic: " Another day they deliberated before the emperor, who asked who could serve as chief minister; Chonghui named Xie.

sentences.zh: 圜曰：「重誨未悉朝中人物，為人所賣。

translations.literal: Huan said, "Chonghui does not know the figures at court and is being sold by others.
translations.idiomatic: Huan said, "Chonghui does not know the figures at court and is being misled.

sentences.zh: 協雖名家，識字甚少。

translations.literal: Xie, though from a famous family, knows very few characters.
translations.idiomatic: Xie, though from a famous family, can barely read.

sentences.zh: 臣既以不學忝相位，奈何更益以協，為天下笑乎！

translations.literal: I, having disgraced the chief minister's post through lack of learning—how can we add Xie and become the world's laughingstock!
translations.idiomatic: I already disgrace the chief minister's post through lack of learning—how can we add Xie and become the laughingstock of the realm!

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「宰相重任，卿輩更審議之。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "The chief minister's burden is heavy—you must deliberate further.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "The chief minister's post is a heavy burden—deliberate further.

sentences.zh: 吾在河東時見馮書記多才博學，與物無競，此可相矣。

translations.literal: When I was in Hedong I saw Secretary Feng—talented and broadly learned, without contention with others—he can serve as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When I was in Hedong I knew Secretary Feng—talented, learned, and without personal ambition—he can serve as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 」既退，孔循不揖，拂衣徑去，曰：「天下事一則任圜，二則任圜，圜何者！

translations.literal: " After they withdrew, Kong Xun did not bow but brushed his robe and went straight out, saying, "The realm's affairs: first Ren Huan, second Ren Huan—what is Ren Huan!
translations.idiomatic: " After they withdrew, Kong Xun did not bow but brushed his robe and stalked out, saying, "The realm's affairs: first Ren Huan, second Ren Huan—who is Ren Huan!

sentences.zh: 使崔協暴死則已，不死會須相之。

translations.literal: If only Cui Xie would die suddenly; if he does not die, in time he will have to be made chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: If only Cui Xie would die suddenly; if he does not, he will eventually become chief minister.

sentences.zh: 」因稱疾不朝者數日，上使重誨諭之，方入。

translations.literal: " He therefore claimed illness and did not attend court for several days; the emperor had Chonghui instruct him, and only then did he enter.
translations.idiomatic: " He claimed illness and stayed away from court for several days until the emperor sent Chonghui to summon him back.

sentences.zh: 重誨私謂圜曰：「今方乏人，協且備員，可乎？

translations.literal: Chonghui privately said to Huan, "We are short of men just now—could Xie serve as a placeholder?
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui privately asked Huan, "We are short of men—could Xie serve as a placeholder?

sentences.zh: 」圜曰：「明公捨李琪而相崔協，是猶棄蘇合之丸，取蛣蜣之轉也。

translations.literal: " Huan said, "My lord, if you abandon Li Qi and make Cui Xie chief minister, it is like discarding a ball of storax and taking the rolled dung of a dung beetle.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan said, "My lord, to abandon Li Qi for Cui Xie is like discarding storax incense for a ball of dung.

sentences.zh: 」循與重誨共事，日短琪而譽協，癸亥，竟以端明殿學士馮道及崔協並為中書議郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: " Xun and Chonghui worked together, daily belittling Qi and praising Xie. On the day guihai, Feng Dao, academician of the Duanming Hall, and Cui Xie were at last both made councilor of the Secretariat and co-equal chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: " Xun and Chonghui worked together, daily belittling Qi and praising Xie. On guihai day Feng Dao, Duanming Hall academician, and Cui Xie were both made councilor of the Secretariat and co-equal chief minister.

sentences.zh: 協，邠之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Xie was a great-grandson of Cui Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Xie was a great-grandson of Cui Bin.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，王延稟還建州，王延鈞送之，將別，謂延鈞曰：「善守先人基業，勿煩老兄再下！

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, Wang Yanbing returned to Jianzhou. Wang Yanjun escorted him; as they were about to part, he said to Yanjun, "Guard our forefathers' foundation well—do not trouble your elder brother to come down again!
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day Wang Yanbing returned to Jianzhou. Wang Yanjun escorted him and as they parted said, "Guard our forefathers' foundation well—do not make your elder brother march south again!

sentences.zh: 」延鈞遜謝甚恭而色變。

translations.literal: " Yanjun apologized with great courtesy, but his expression changed.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanjun apologized with great courtesy, but his expression darkened.

sentences.zh: 庚午，初令天下長吏每旬親引慮系囚。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, for the first time chief local officials throughout the realm were ordered every ten days personally to review prisoners awaiting judgment.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day the emperor for the first time ordered chief local officials throughout the realm to review prisoners awaiting judgment every ten days.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥禮遇李嚴甚厚，一日謁知祥，知祥謂曰：「公前奉使王衍，歸而請兵伐蜀，莊宗用公言，遂致兩國俱亡。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang treated Li Yan with great courtesy. One day Yan called on Zhixiang, who said to him, "Sir, you earlier served as envoy to Wang Yan, returned, and asked for troops to attack Shu. Zhuangzong followed your advice, and both states perished.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang treated Li Yan with great courtesy. One day Yan called on him, and Zhixiang said, "You once served as envoy to Wang Yan, returned, and urged an attack on Shu. Zhuangzong followed your advice, and both states were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 今公復來，蜀人懼矣。

translations.literal: Now you come again—the people of Shu are afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Now you come again, and the people of Shu are afraid.

sentences.zh: 且天下皆廢監軍，公獨來監吾軍，何也？

translations.literal: Moreover, military supervisors have been abolished throughout the realm—why do you alone come to supervise my army?
translations.idiomatic: Military supervisors have been abolished throughout the realm—why do you alone come to supervise my army?

sentences.zh: 」嚴惶怖求哀，知祥曰：「眾怒不可遏也。

translations.literal: " Yan was terrified and begged for mercy. Zhixiang said, "The people's anger cannot be restrained.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan was terrified and begged for mercy. Zhixiang said, "The people's anger cannot be restrained.

sentences.zh: 」遂揖下，斬之。

translations.literal: " He then had him led down and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: " He had him led down and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 又召左廂馬步都虞候丁知俊，知俊大懼，知祥指嚴屍謂曰：「昔嚴奉使，汝為之副，然則故人也，為我瘞之。

translations.literal: He then summoned Ding Zhijun, chief adjutant of the left wing horse and foot. Zhijun was greatly afraid. Zhixiang pointed at Yan's corpse and said, "In the past when Yan served as envoy, you were his deputy—you are an old acquaintance; bury him for me.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Ding Zhijun, chief adjutant of the left wing. Zhijun was terrified. Zhixiang pointed at Yan's corpse and said, "When Yan served as envoy you were his deputy—you are an old friend; bury him for me.

sentences.zh: 」因誣奏：「嚴詐宣口敕，雲代臣赴闕，又擅許將士優賞，臣輒已誅之。

translations.literal: " He then falsely memorialized, "Yan fraudulently announced an oral edict saying he would replace me and go to court, and on his own authority promised the soldiers generous rewards; your servant has already executed him.
translations.idiomatic: " He then falsely memorialized that Yan had forged an oral edict claiming he would replace Zhixiang at court and had on his own authority promised the troops generous rewards, and that he had executed him.

sentences.zh: 」內八作使楊令芝以事入蜀，至鹿頭關，聞嚴死，奔還。

translations.literal: " Yang Lingzhi, commissioner of the inner eight workshops, entered Shu on business; when he reached Lutou Pass and heard of Yan's death, he fled back.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Lingzhi, commissioner of the inner eight workshops, was entering Shu on business; when he reached Lutou Pass and heard of Yan's death, he fled back.

sentences.zh: 朱弘昭在東川，聞之，亦懼，謀歸洛；

translations.literal: Zhu Hongzhao was in Dongchuan; hearing of it, he too was afraid and planned to return to Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hongzhao was in Dongchuan; hearing of it, he too was afraid and planned to return to Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 會有軍事，董璋使之入奏，弘照偽辭然後行，由是得免。

translations.literal: when military affairs arose, Dong Zhang had him enter court to report; Hongzhao made a false excuse and then departed, and thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: when military affairs arose Dong Zhang had him report to court; Hongzhao made a false excuse and departed, and thereby escaped.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以皇子從厚同平章事，充河南尹，判六軍諸衛事。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, the imperial prince Conghou was made co-equal chief minister, filled the post of Henan prefect, and held charge of the six armies and various guards.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day the imperial prince Conghou was made co-equal chief minister, Henan prefect, and overseer of the six armies and various guards.

sentences.zh: 從厚，從榮之母弟也。

translations.literal: Conghou was Congrong's younger brother by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: Conghou was Congrong's younger brother by the same mother.

sentences.zh: 從榮聞之，不悅。

translations.literal: When Congrong heard of it, he was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Congrong was displeased when he heard.

sentences.zh: 己卯，加樞密使安重誨兼侍中，孔循同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day jimao, chief palace secretary An Chonghui was given the additional title of palace attendant, and Kong Xun was made co-equal chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day An Chonghui, chief palace secretary, was made concurrent palace attendant, and Kong Xun was made co-equal chief minister.

sentences.zh: 吳馬軍都指揮使柴再用戎服入朝，御史彈之，再用恃功不服。

translations.literal: Chai Zaiyong, commander of the Wu horse army, entered court in military dress; the censor impeached him, and Zaiyong relied on his merit and would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Zaiyong, Wu commander of the horse army, entered court in military dress; the censor impeached him, but Zaiyong relied on his merit and refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 侍中徐知誥陽於便殿誤通起居，退而自劾，吳王優詔不問。

translations.literal: Palace attendant Xu Zhihao, at the informal hall, mistakenly announced himself in the audience ritual; he withdrew and impeached himself, and the King of Wu issued a gracious edict and did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Xu Zhihao mistakenly announced himself at the informal hall; he withdrew and impeached himself, and the King of Wu graciously declined to punish him.

sentences.zh: 知誥固請奪一月俸；

translations.literal: Zhihao firmly asked that one month's salary be taken from him;
translations.idiomatic: Zhihao firmly asked that one month's salary be deducted;

sentences.zh: 由是中外肅然。

translations.literal: from this within and without the court were all in awe.
translations.idiomatic: from this the court and the realm were awed into order.

sentences.zh: 契丹改元天顯，葬其主阿保機於木葉山。

translations.literal: The Khitan changed the era name to Tianxian and buried their ruler Abaoji at Mount Muye.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan changed the era name to Tianxian and buried Abaoji at Mount Muye.

sentences.zh: 述律太后左右有桀黠者，後輒謂曰：「為我達語於先帝！

translations.literal: Among those at Empress Shulü's side were fierce and cunning men; the empress would say to them, "Convey my words to the late emperor!
translations.idiomatic: Among those at Empress Shulü's side were fierce and cunning men; she would tell them, "Convey my words to the late emperor!

sentences.zh: 」至墓所則殺之，前後所殺以百數。

translations.literal: " When they reached the tomb site she killed them; those killed before and after numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: " When they reached the tomb she killed them; the victims numbered in the hundreds.

sentences.zh: 最後，平州人趙思溫當往，思溫不行，後曰：「汝事先帝嘗親近，何為不行？

translations.literal: At last Zhao Siwen of Pingzhou was due to go; Siwen would not go. The empress said, "You served the late emperor and were once close to him—why will you not go?
translations.idiomatic: At last Zhao Siwen of Pingzhou was due to go, but he refused. The empress said, "You were close to the late emperor—why will you not go?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「親近莫如-{后}-，-{后}-行，臣則繼之。

translations.literal: " The reply was, "No one was closer than Your Majesty—if Your Majesty goes, your servant will follow.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "No one was closer than Your Majesty—if Your Majesty goes, I will follow.

sentences.zh: 」後曰：「吾非不欲從先帝於地下也，顧嗣子幼弱，國家無主，不得往耳。

translations.literal: " The empress said, "It is not that I do not wish to follow the late emperor underground, but considering that the heir is young and weak and the state has no lord, I cannot go.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress said, "It is not that I do not wish to follow the late emperor underground, but the heir is young and the state has no ruler—I cannot go.

sentences.zh: 」乃斷一腕，令置墓中。

translations.literal: " She then cut off one wrist and ordered it placed in the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: " She cut off one wrist and ordered it placed in the tomb.

sentences.zh: 思溫亦得免。

translations.literal: Siwen also escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Siwen was spared as well.

sentences.zh: 帝以冀州刺史烏震三將兵運糧入幽州，二月，戊子，以震為河北道副招討，領寧國節度使，屯盧台軍。

translations.literal: Because Wu Zhensan, prefect of Jizhou, was leading troops to transport grain into Youzhou, in the second month, on the day wuzi, Zhensan was made deputy commander for the Hebei circuit, concurrent military governor of Ningguo, and stationed at the Lutai army.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wu Zhensan, prefect of Jizhou, was transporting grain to Youzhou, in the second month, on wuzi day, he was made deputy commander for Hebei, concurrent military governor of Ningguo, stationed at the Lutai army.

sentences.zh: 代泰寧節度使、同平章事房知溫歸兗州。

translations.literal: He replaced Fang Zhiwen, military governor of Taining and co-equal chief minister, who returned to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced Fang Zhiwen, military governor of Taining and co-equal chief minister, who returned to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以保義節度使石敬瑭兼六軍諸衛副使。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin, Shi Jingtang, military governor of Baoyi, was made concurrent deputy overseer of the six armies and various guards.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day Shi Jingtang, military governor of Baoyi, was made deputy overseer of the six armies and various guards.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以從馬直指揮使郭從謙為景州刺史，既至，遣使族誅之。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, Guo Congqian, commander of the Imperial Horse Direct Advance Guard, was made prefect of Jingzhou; once he arrived, an envoy was sent to execute his entire clan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day Guo Congqian, commander of the Imperial Horse Direct Advance Guard, was appointed prefect of Jingzhou; once he arrived, the court sent envoys to execute his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 高季興既得三州，請朝廷不除刺史，自以子弟為之，不許。

translations.literal: After Gao Jixing obtained the three prefectures, he asked that the court not appoint prefects and that he install his own sons and younger brothers; permission was refused.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao Jixing obtained the three prefectures, he asked that the court not appoint prefects so he could install his own kin; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 及夔州刺史潘炕罷官，季興輒遣兵突入州城，殺戍兵而據之。

translations.literal: When Pan Kang, prefect of Kuizhou, left office, Jixing promptly sent troops to burst into the prefectural city, kill the garrison troops, and seize it.
translations.idiomatic: When Pan Kang, prefect of Kuizhou, left office, Jixing sent troops to burst into the city, kill the garrison, and seize it.

sentences.zh: 朝廷除奉聖指揮使西方鄴為刺史，不受；

translations.literal: The court appointed Xifang Ye, commander of the Fengsheng Guard, prefect; he was not accepted;
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Xifang Ye, commander of the Fengsheng Guard, prefect; Jixing refused;

sentences.zh: 又遣兵襲涪州，不克。

translations.literal: troops were again sent to raid Fuzhou but did not capture it.
translations.idiomatic: and sent troops to raid Fuzhou but failed to capture it.

sentences.zh: 魏王繼岌遣押牙韓珙等部送蜀珍貨金帛四十萬，浮江而下，季興殺珙等於峽口，盡掠取之。

translations.literal: Prince of Wei Li Jiji had sent Han Gong and others of the guard to escort four hundred thousand in Shu treasures and silks downstream by river; Jixing killed Gong and the others at the gorge mouth and plundered everything.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei Li Jiji had sent Han Gong and others to escort four hundred thousand in Shu treasures downstream by river; Jixing killed them at the gorge mouth and plundered everything.

sentences.zh: 朝廷詰之，對曰：「珙等舟行下峽，涉數千里，欲知覆溺之故，自宜按問水神。

translations.literal: The court questioned him. He replied, "Gong and the others traveled downstream through the gorge for several thousand li—if you wish to know the cause of capsizing and drowning, you should naturally inquire of the water god.
translations.idiomatic: The court questioned him. He replied, "Gong and the others traveled downstream through the gorge for thousands of li—if you wish to know why they capsized, you should inquire of the water god.

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，壬寅，制削奪季興官爵，以山南東道節度使劉訓為南面招討使、知荊南行府事，忠武節度使夏魯奇為副招討使，將步騎四萬討之。

translations.literal: " The emperor was angry. On the day renyin an edict stripped Jixing of titles and offices. Liu Xun, military governor of Shannan East Circuit, was made southern campaign commander and administrator of the Jingnan expedition headquarters; Xia Luqi, military governor of Zhongwu, was made deputy commander, leading forty thousand foot and horse to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was furious. On renyin day an edict stripped Jixing of his titles. Liu Xun, military governor of Shannan East, was made southern campaign commander; Xia Luqi of Zhongwu was deputy commander, leading forty thousand troops against him.

sentences.zh: 東川節度使董璋充東南面招討使，新夔州刺史西方鄴副之，將蜀兵下峽，仍會湖南軍三面進攻。

translations.literal: Dong Zhang, military governor of Dongchuan, served as southeastern campaign commander, with the new Kuizhou prefect Xifang Ye as deputy; they led Shu troops down the gorge and joined Hunan forces in a three-sided attack.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang of Dongchuan served as southeastern campaign commander with the new Kuizhou prefect Xifang Ye as deputy; they led Shu troops down the gorge and joined Hunan forces in a three-sided attack.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲寅，以李敬周為武信留後。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day jiayin, Li Jingzhou was made acting prefect of Wuxin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiayin day, Li Jingzhou was made acting prefect of Wuxin.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，初置監牧，蕃息國馬。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, pasture supervision was first established to breed state horses.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day pasture supervision was first established to breed state horses.

sentences.zh: 初，莊宗之克梁也，以魏州牙兵之力；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhuangzong conquered the Liang, it was through the strength of the Ye Capital guard troops;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhuangzong conquered the Liang, it was through the Ye guard troops;

sentences.zh: 及其亡也，皇甫暉、張破敗之亂亦由之。

translations.literal: when he perished, the disorders of Huangfu Hui and Zhang Popo also came from them.
translations.idiomatic: when he fell, the disorders of Huangfu Hui and Zhang Popo also came from them.

sentences.zh: 趙在禮之徙滑州，不之官，亦實為其下所制。

translations.literal: When Zhao Zaili was transferred to Huazhou and did not take up his post, he too was in fact controlled by his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Zaili was transferred to Huazhou and did not take up his post, he too was controlled by his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 在禮欲自謀脫禍，陰遣腹心詣闕求移鎮，帝乃為之除皇甫暉陳州刺史，趙進貝州刺史，趙在禮為橫海節度使；

translations.literal: Zaili wished to extricate himself from disaster and secretly sent trusted men to court to seek a transfer of post. The emperor then appointed Huangfu Hui prefect of Chenzhou, Zhao Jin prefect of Beizhou, and Zhao Zaili military governor of Henghai;
translations.idiomatic: Zaili sought to escape and secretly sent trusted men to court to seek transfers. The emperor appointed Huangfu Hui prefect of Chenzhou, Zhao Jin prefect of Beizhou, and Zhao Zaili military governor of Henghai;

sentences.zh: 以皇子從榮鎮鄴都，命宣徽北院使范延光將兵送之，且制置鄴都軍事。

translations.literal: the imperial prince Congrong was stationed at Ye Capital; Fan Yanguang, commissioner of the northern bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was ordered to lead troops to escort him and also arrange Ye Capital military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: the imperial prince Congrong was stationed at Ye Capital; Fan Yanguang, northern bureau commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, escorted him and arranged Ye military affairs.

sentences.zh: 乃出奉節等九指揮三千五百人，使軍校龍晊部之，戍盧台軍以備契丹，不給鎧仗，但系幟於長竿以別隊伍，由是皆俛首而去。

translations.literal: Then three thousand five hundred men of nine commands including Fengjie were released, with the army officer Long Zhi leading them to garrison the Lutai army against the Khitan; no armor or weapons were issued—only banners on long poles to distinguish units—and thereby all bowed their heads and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand five hundred men of nine commands including Fengjie were released under the officer Long Zhi to garrison Lutai against the Khitan. They received no armor or weapons—only banners on long poles to mark their units—and bowed their heads and departed.

sentences.zh: 中塗聞孟知祥殺李嚴，軍中籍籍，已有訛言；

translations.literal: Midway they heard that Meng Zhixiang had killed Li Yan; in the army there was murmuring and already false reports;
translations.idiomatic: Midway they heard that Meng Zhixiang had killed Li Yan; the army murmured and rumors spread;

sentences.zh: 既至，會朝延不次擢烏震為副招討使，訛言益甚。

translations.literal: when they arrived, it happened that the court had abruptly promoted Wu Zhensan to deputy campaign commander, and the false reports grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: when they arrived the court had abruptly promoted Wu Zhensan to deputy campaign commander, and the rumors grew worse.

sentences.zh: 房知溫怨震驟來代己，震至，未交印。

translations.literal: Fang Zhiwen resented that Zhensan had suddenly come to replace him. When Zhensan arrived, the seals had not yet been exchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Zhiwen resented Zhensan's sudden arrival to replace him. When Zhensan arrived, the seals had not yet been exchanged.

sentences.zh: 壬申，震召知溫及諸道先鋒馬軍都指揮使、齊州防禦使安神博於東寨，知溫誘龍晊所部兵殺震於席上，其眾噪於營外，安審通脫身走，奪舟濟河，將騎兵按甲不動。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, Zhensan summoned Zhiwen and An Shenbo, commander of the vanguard horse army of the various circuits and defense commissioner of Qizhou, to the eastern camp. Zhiwen induced Long Zhi's troops to kill Zhensan at the banquet. Their followers clamored outside the camp. An Shentong escaped, seized a boat and crossed the river, and led the cavalry with armor undisturbed.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day Zhensan summoned Zhiwen and An Shenbo, vanguard horse commander and defense commissioner of Qizhou, to the eastern camp. Zhiwen induced Long Zhi's troops to kill Zhensan at the banquet. The mutineers clamored outside camp. An Shentong escaped by boat across the river while the cavalry held their position.

sentences.zh: 知溫恐事不濟，亦上馬出門，軍士攬其轡曰：「公當為士卒主，去欲何之？

translations.literal: Zhiwen feared matters would not succeed and also mounted his horse to leave the gate. Soldiers seized his bridle and said, "You should be master of the soldiers—where do you mean to go?
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen feared failure and mounted his horse to flee. Soldiers seized his bridle: "You are our leader—where are you going?

sentences.zh: 」知溫給之曰：「騎兵皆在河西，不收取之，獨有步兵，何能集事！

translations.literal: " Zhiwen deceived them, saying, "The cavalry are all west of the river—if we do not gather them in, with infantry alone how can we accomplish the affair!
translations.idiomatic: " Zhiwen deceived them: "The cavalry are west of the river—without them, how can infantry alone succeed!

sentences.zh: 」遂躍馬登舟濟河，與審通合謀擊亂兵，亂兵遂南行。

translations.literal: " He then leaped on his horse, boarded a boat, crossed the river, joined Shentong in plotting to strike the mutineers, and the mutineers thereupon marched south.
translations.idiomatic: " He leaped on his horse, boarded a boat, crossed the river, joined Shentong to strike the mutineers, and the mutineers marched south.

sentences.zh: 騎兵徐踵其後，部伍甚整。

translations.literal: The cavalry followed slowly behind them, their formations very orderly.
translations.idiomatic: The cavalry followed slowly behind in perfect order.

sentences.zh: 亂者相顧失色，列炬宵行，疲於荒澤，詰朝，騎兵四合擊之，亂兵殆盡，餘眾復趣故寨，審通已焚之，亂兵進退失據，遂潰。

translations.literal: The mutineers looked at one another in dismay, marched by torchlight through the night, and were exhausted in the wild marshes. At dawn the cavalry closed in from four sides and struck them; the mutineers were nearly all destroyed. The remainder turned back toward their old camp, but Shentong had already burned it; the mutineers lost their footing advance and retreat and then broke apart.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers looked at one another in dismay and marched by torchlight through wild marshes until dawn, when the cavalry closed in from four sides and nearly destroyed them. The remainder turned back toward their old camp, but Shentong had burned it; with nowhere to turn, they broke apart.

sentences.zh: 其匿於叢薄溝塍得免者什無一二。

translations.literal: Of those who hid in thickets, ditches, and furrows and escaped, not one in ten survived.
translations.idiomatic: Of those who hid in thickets and ditches, fewer than one in ten escaped.

sentences.zh: 范延光還至淇門，聞盧台亂，發滑州兵復如鄴都，以備奔逸。

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang returned to Qimen; hearing of the Lutai mutiny, he mobilized Huazhou troops and again went to Ye Capital to guard against fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang returned to Qimen; hearing of the Lutai mutiny, he mobilized Huazhou troops and marched to Ye Capital to block fugitives.

sentences.zh: 帝遣客省使李仁矩如西川，傳詔安諭孟知祥及吏民；

translations.literal: The emperor sent Li Renju, commissioner of the Reception Bureau, to Xichuan to convey an edict comforting and reassuring Meng Zhixiang and officials and people;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Li Renju, commissioner of the Reception Bureau, to Xichuan with an edict reassuring Meng Zhixiang and the officials and people;

sentences.zh: 甲戌，至成都。

translations.literal: on the day jiaxu he reached Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: on jiaxu day he reached Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 劉訓兵至荊南，楚王殷遣都指揮使許德勳等將水軍屯岳州。

translations.literal: When Liu Xun's army reached Jingnan, Prince Chu Yin sent Xu Dexun, commander-in-chief, and others to lead the naval army and encamp at Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xun's army reached Jingnan, Prince Chu Yin sent Xu Dexun and others with the naval army to encamp at Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 高秀興堅壁不戰，求救於吳，吳人遣水軍援之。

translations.literal: Gao Jixing held his walls and would not fight, asked Wu for rescue, and the Wu sent a naval army to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jixing held his walls and would not fight, asked Wu for aid, and Wu sent a naval force to help him.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚寅，敕盧台亂兵在營家屬並全門處斬。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day gengyin, an edict ordered that the families of the Lutai mutineers still in camp be executed to the last household.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on gengyin day an edict ordered the families of the Lutai mutineers still in camp executed to the last household.

sentences.zh: 敕至鄴都，闔九指揮之門，驅三千五百家凡萬餘人於石灰窯，悉斬之，永濟渠為之變赤。

translations.literal: When the edict reached Ye Capital, the doors of all nine commands were closed; three thousand five hundred households, more than ten thousand people in all, were driven to the lime kilns and all beheaded; the Yongji Canal turned red from it.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict reached Ye Capital, the doors of all nine commands were sealed; three thousand five hundred households, more than ten thousand people, were driven to the lime kilns and beheaded; the Yongji Canal ran red.

sentences.zh: 朝廷雖知房知溫首亂，欲安反仄，癸巳，加知溫兼侍中。

translations.literal: Although the court knew that Fang Zhiwen had led the mutiny and wished to settle unrest, on the day guisi he was given the additional title of palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Although the court knew Fang Zhiwen had led the mutiny and wished to settle unrest, on guisi day he was made concurrent palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 先是，孟知祥遣牙內指揮使文水武漳迎其妻瓊華長公主及子仁贊於晉陽，及鳳翔，李從曮聞知祥殺李嚴，止之，以聞，帝聽其歸蜀；

translations.literal: Earlier, Meng Zhixiang had sent Wu Zhang of Wenshui, commander of the inner guard, to welcome his wife Princess Qionghua and his son Renzan from Taiyuan; when they reached Fengxiang, Li Congyao heard that Zhixiang had killed Li Yan, stopped them, and reported it; the emperor permitted them to return to Shu;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Meng Zhixiang had sent Wu Zhang of Wenshui to welcome his wife Princess Qionghua and his son Renzan from Taiyuan; at Fengxiang Li Congyao, hearing that Zhixiang had killed Li Yan, stopped them and reported it; the emperor permitted them to return to Shu;

sentences.zh: 丙申，至成都。

translations.literal: on the day bingshen they reached Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: on bingshen day they reached Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 鹽鐵判官趙季良與孟知祥有舊，知祥奏留季良為副使。

translations.literal: Zhao Jiliang, salt-and-iron commissioner, was an old acquaintance of Meng Zhixiang; Zhixiang memorialized to retain Jiliang as deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jiliang, salt-and-iron commissioner, was an old friend of Meng Zhixiang, who memorialized to keep him as deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不得已，丁酉，以季良為西川節度副使。

translations.literal: The court had no choice; on the day dingyou, Jiliang was made vice military governor of Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: The court had no choice; on dingyou day Jiliang was appointed vice military governor of Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 李昊歸蜀，知祥以為觀察推官。

translations.literal: Li Hao returned to Shu; Zhixiang made him legal officer of the observation commission.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hao returned to Shu, and Zhixiang appointed him legal officer of the observation commission.

sentences.zh: 江陵卑濕，復值久雨，糧道不繼，將士疾疫，劉訓亦寢疾；

translations.literal: Jiangling was low and damp; prolonged rain again made supply lines fail, soldiers and officers fell to pestilence, and Liu Xun also took to his bed with illness;
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling was low and damp; prolonged rain cut the supply lines, troops fell to pestilence, and Liu Xun himself fell ill;

sentences.zh: 癸卯，帝遣樞密使孔循往視之，且審攻戰之宜。

translations.literal: on the day guimao the emperor sent chief palace secretary Kong Xun to inspect the situation and assess what was fitting for attack and battle.
translations.idiomatic: on guimao day the emperor sent Kong Xun, chief palace secretary, to inspect the situation and decide whether to continue the campaign.

sentences.zh: 五月，癸丑，以威武留後王延鈞為本道節度使、守中書令、琅邪王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day guichou, Wang Yanjun, acting prefect of Weiwu, was made military governor of his circuit, guardian of the Secretariat, and Prince of Langya.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guichou day, Wang Yanjun, acting prefect of Weiwu, was made military governor of his circuit, guardian of the Secretariat, and Prince of Langya.

sentences.zh: 孔循至江陵，攻之不克，遣人入城說高季興；

translations.literal: Kong Xun reached Jiangling but could not capture it; he sent someone into the city to persuade Gao Jixing;
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xun reached Jiangling but could not take it; he sent envoys into the city to persuade Gao Jixing;

sentences.zh: 季興不遜。

translations.literal: Jixing was insubordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Jixing was defiant.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，遣使賜湖南行營夏衣萬襲；

translations.literal: on the day bingyin envoys were sent to grant ten thousand summer garments to the Hunan expedition camp;
translations.idiomatic: on bingyin day envoys were sent with ten thousand summer garments for the Hunan expedition;

sentences.zh: 丁卯，又遣使賜楚王殷鞍馬玉帶，督饋糧於行營，竟不能得。

translations.literal: on the day dingmao envoys were again sent to grant Prince Chu Yin saddled horses and a jade belt and to press for grain deliveries to the expedition camp, but in the end none could be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: on dingmao day envoys were sent again with saddled horses and a jade belt for Prince Chu Yin and to press for grain for the expedition, but none was delivered.

sentences.zh: 庚午，詔劉訓等引兵還。

translations.literal: on the day gengwu an edict ordered Liu Xun and the others to withdraw their troops.
translations.idiomatic: on gengwu day an edict ordered Liu Xun and the others to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 楚王殷遣中軍使史光憲入貢，帝賜之駿馬十，美女二。

translations.literal: Prince Chu Yin sent Shi Guangxian, commissioner of the central army, to present tribute; the emperor granted him ten fine horses and two beautiful women.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chu Yin sent Shi Guangxian, commissioner of the central army, to present tribute; the emperor gave him ten fine horses and two beautiful women.

sentences.zh: 過江陵，高季興執光憲而奪之，且請舉鎮自附於吳。

translations.literal: Passing Jiangling, Gao Jixing seized Guangxian and took the gifts, and also asked to bring his whole commandery and submit to Wu of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Jiangling, Gao Jixing seized Guangxian and took the gifts, and asked to submit his whole commandery to Wu.

sentences.zh: 徐溫曰：「為國者當務實效而去虛名。

translations.literal: Xu Wen said, "One who governs a state should pursue real effect and discard empty names.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen said, "A ruler should pursue real effect and discard empty names.

sentences.zh: 高氏事唐久矣，洛陽去江陵不遠，唐人步騎襲之甚易，我以舟師溯流救之甚難。

translations.literal: The Gao clan has served Tang for a long time; Luoyang is not far from Jiangling—Tang foot and horse could strike them very easily, while our naval forces going upstream to rescue them would be very hard.
translations.idiomatic: The Gao clan has served Tang for a long time. Luoyang is not far from Jiangling—Tang infantry and cavalry could strike them easily, while our fleet going upstream to rescue them would be very hard.

sentences.zh: 夫臣人而弗能救，使之危亡，能無愧乎！

translations.literal: To accept someone as a subject and yet be unable to save him, letting him fall into peril and ruin—can one be without shame!
translations.idiomatic: To accept someone as a subject and be unable to save him when he falls into peril—how could we not be ashamed!

sentences.zh: 」乃受其貢物，辭其稱臣，聽其自附於唐。

translations.literal: " He therefore accepted his tribute goods, declined his offer of subjection, and permitted him to submit to Tang on his own.
translations.idiomatic: " He accepted the tribute goods, declined the offer of subjection, and permitted Jixing to submit to Tang on his own.

sentences.zh: 任圜性剛直，且恃與帝有舊，勇於敢為，權幸多疾之。

translations.literal: Ren Huan was upright and blunt by nature, and relying on his old ties with the emperor, he was bold in action; many of the powerful resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Huan was blunt and upright by nature and, relying on his old ties with the emperor, acted boldly; many at court resented him.

sentences.zh: 舊制，館券出於戶部，安重誨請從內出，與圜爭於上前，往複數四，聲色俱厲。

translations.literal: By old regulation, lodging vouchers came from the Ministry of Revenue; An Chonghui asked that they come from the inner court and argued with Huan before the emperor back and forth several times, both voice and expression fierce.
translations.idiomatic: By old regulation lodging vouchers came from the Ministry of Revenue; An Chonghui asked that they come from the inner court and argued with Huan before the emperor several times, both men fierce in voice and expression.

sentences.zh: 上退朝，宮人問上：「適與重誨論事為誰？

translations.literal: After the emperor left court, a palace woman asked him, "With whom were you just now discussing affairs with Chonghui?
translations.idiomatic: After court a palace woman asked the emperor, "With whom were you just arguing with Chonghui?

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「宰相。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "The chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "The chief minister.

sentences.zh: 」宮人曰：「妾在長安宮中，未嘗見宰相、樞密奏事敢如是者，蓋輕大家耳。

translations.literal: " The palace woman said, "When I was in the Chang'an palace, I never saw a chief minister or palace secretary present business so boldly—they must look down on Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: " The palace woman said, "In the Chang'an palace I never saw a chief minister or palace secretary present business so boldly—they must look down on Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」上愈不悅，卒從重誨議。

translations.literal: " The emperor grew still more displeased and at last followed Chonghui's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor grew still more displeased and at last followed Chonghui's proposal.

sentences.zh: 圜因求罷三司，詔以樞密承旨孟鵠充三司副使權判。

translations.literal: Huan therefore asked to resign from the three departments; an edict appointed Meng Hu, palace secretary recipient, provisional deputy commissioner of the three departments with acting charge.
translations.idiomatic: Huan asked to resign from the three departments; an edict appointed Meng Hu, palace secretary recipient, acting deputy commissioner of the three departments.

sentences.zh: 鵠，魏州人也。

translations.literal: Hu was a man of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hu was from Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚辰，太子詹事溫輦請立太子。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day gengchen, Wen Nian, grand mentor of the heir apparent, asked that the heir apparent be formally installed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on gengchen day, Wen Nian, grand mentor of the heir apparent, asked that the heir apparent be formally installed.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，門下侍郎、同平章事任圜罷守太子少保。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, Ren Huan, vice grand councilor of the Chancellery and co-equal chief minister, was dismissed and made junior guardian of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day Ren Huan, vice grand councilor and co-equal chief minister, was dismissed and made junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以宣徽北院使張延朗判三司。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, Zhang Yanlang, commissioner of the northern bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was given charge of the three departments.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day Zhang Yanlang, northern bureau commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, was given charge of the three departments.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，貶劉訓為檀州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, Liu Xun was demoted to prefect of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day Liu Xun was demoted to prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙申，封楚王殷為楚國王。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, Prince Chu Yin was enfeoffed as King of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day Prince Chu Yin was enfeoffed as King of Chu.

sentences.zh: 西方鄴敗荊南水於峽中，復取夔、忠、萬三州。

translations.literal: Xifang Ye defeated the Jingnan navy in the gorge and recovered the three prefectures of Kui, Zhong, and Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Xifang Ye defeated the Jingnan fleet in the gorge and recovered Kui, Zhong, and Wan.

translations.idiomatic: category: Zizhi Tongjian
